issues.body:
Hero run started on August 19th. This should be a terse log of status events and interventions since then.

```
./experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/trigger_hero.sh
```

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
August 20th: noticed that we are OOMing every ~3 hours.

We attempted interventions to adjust XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.83 (giving XLA more memory). This made things worse. 

--xla_gpu_memory_limit_slop_factor seems to be another promising tunable. Adjusting to 0.88 from the default 0.95 didn't help. Testing with 0.85 now.

In theory fraction 0.83 with slop 88 strictly dominates the baseline, as a followup to test if the lowered thresholds don't hold.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
We observed periodic host OOMs after several checkpoints. https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/200 . Restarting with the following changes:

1. Tensorstore restore parallelism bounded by a fixed budget
2. Checkpoint offload cache to 16GB
3. malloc_trim() calls after each checkpoint

in theory 2 will make checkpoints faster (fully async), and 3 will prevent the host OOM recurrence

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
`malloc_trim` was still inconsistently resulting in OOMs during checkpointing. Restarting on main with the jemalloc changes in.

Restores were hitting single worker stalls. Merged and running with #8584 . First restore after this change was successful, though it might have been luck/caching.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Memory sampling on the current `coord-memfix` instance isolates checkpoint-correlated retained RSS to writer tasks 0–127. Their median floor rose 11.7 GiB after the first save and 4.4 GiB after the second; tasks 128–175 stayed on the baseline slope. Each writer rank was assigned about 9.5–10.2 GiB, and `/proc` attributes the retained difference to anonymous memory across the four child Python processes.

The run contains #8609. The signature matches its documented persistent CUDA pinned-host BFC pool cost. The smaller second increment does not support projecting a fixed 30 GiB leak per save.

Incident record: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/227

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 Correction after tracing the current checkpoint path: the long-lived `GlobalAsyncCheckpointManager` keeps the completed TensorStore commit futures in `_commit_futures`; `wait_until_finished()` joins but does not clear them, and the writes allow indefinite source-buffer references. This mechanism predates #8609 and plausibly retains one staged checkpoint share per writer rank. PR #8599 contained a reviewed post-join cleanup for these futures, but that part did not land with #8609. The pinned-host BFC pool in #8609 remains an additional allocator-level floor that clearing the manager cannot purge. Updated evidence and safe cleanup boundaries: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/227

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body: 🤖 The loader-cache ablation is complete. On two trays with the Harrier mixture, global batch 1024, and sequence length 4096, the profiler-free 1 GB/process arm delivered 0.937 batches/s including cold start versus 0.956 batches/s at 125 GB/process. The hero runs at 19.9 s/step (0.050 batches/s), so the 1 GB cap has 18.6x headroom and bounds the decoded cache near 0.923 GiB/process. Report: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/235

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Paused for the #8870 debugging window and redeployed from main. A checkpoint was forced through the training-control endpoint before the cancel, so the pause cost about one step instead of the ~131 (~44 min, ~515 GPU-hours) that killing at a random point in the hourly temporary-checkpoint cycle would have discarded: `step-58014` committed 23:13:13Z and was verified complete (`manifest.json`, `manifest.ocdbt`, `metadata.json`, 28,098 objects, 5.36 TB). `/marin/hero-12d8b6f0-dee637-coord-e3052688` was cancelled at 23:14:12Z having last logged step 58.0k at loss 1.22.

The window ran 11 racks from 23:16Z to 00:40Z across two jobs and did not reproduce the hang: 164 steps then 71, 235 in total, at the hero's exact shape restored from the same `step-54000` the two failed attempts used. Details in #8870.

Redeployed at 00:41:36Z from a pristine worktree at `origin/main` `023ed7a24d` as `/marin/hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k-coord-95c15d9b`, run id `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k`, submitted with `IRIS_USER=marin`. It carries two changes relative to the paused run: the pooled-wave fallback (#8884, which the paused run was already effectively running) and gate/router weight decay on by default at 0.02 annealed linearly to zero (#8833). The launch args were diffed against the paused run's own recorded argv and match on every field except run id, job name, `--initialize-from-checkpoint`, and the `--system-reason` string.

Resume verified: the gang placed in ~80 s, 177 tasks, and the restore names `step-58014` under the temporary root rather than falling back to the `step-54000` permanent, which would have discarded ~4,000 steps. First step 00:50:12Z; now training at ~18.4 s/step, MFU ~21%, loss ~1.24, continuous with the 1.22-1.25 before the pause, and logging to W&B as `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k`.

Net cost: ~96 min of the 11 racks, of which ~84 was the window and ~9 startup.

Note for #8833: that experiment's launcher originally handed off from `step-54000`; #8890 repointed it at `step-58014` so the relaunch would not discard the day of training since. Its control is therefore the paused hero's own trajectory from 58014, not the step-54000 one.

comments.author: mcwitt
comments.body:
🤖 Plan for today's redeployment of the hero on the ragged all-to-all transport, 2026-09-09. The live run `hero-wd-gate-router-p02-step58k` (commit `0908920c86`) is at step ~81.5k at 19.8 s/step, loss ~1.23.

Sequence: merge #8959 (QuACK 0.6.4, the grouped-GEMM scheduler fix) and #9043 (ragged transport and fp32 weights on device back as the hero default, reverting #8884), then force a checkpoint on the live run through the training-control endpoint about 70 minutes before the cutover, mark its metadata non-temporary so the hourly temporary save does not prune it, open the launcher PR pointing `trigger_hero.sh` at it under run id `hero-ragged_a2a-ep-step<N>k`, let the old run train 200 steps past it as the paired control, cancel the old coordinator, and launch main from a pristine worktree as `IRIS_USER=marin`. Waiting for the next permanent checkpoint was rejected: step-84000 lands at ~07:00Z tomorrow and step-90000 on Thursday, and a forced checkpoint costs one step (the step-58014 precedent).

The new run carries, relative to the live one: the ragged transport with fp32 weights on device (#9043), one train-step executable per rank (#8911), the balanced ragged device kernel wheel (#8976), QuACK 0.6.4 (#8959), and the cross-entropy tile and FA4 padding fixes (#8960, #8961). The root cause of #8870 is still open; the strongest lead is a fabric fault on the racks that land at replica indices 8-10, which the trial cannot avoid.

Gate over the 200-step window against the old run on the same batches: loss within bf16 noise of the control after the ~0.006 nat dropless offset, drop fraction below 1e-3, MFU at or above the control's ~21%, no hang, retry, or watchdog. Anything short of that rolls back at once by relaunching `trigger_hero.sh` at `0908920c86`, which resumes the old run's own newest checkpoint. Runbook scripts (preflight with an NVLink counter sweep, cancel, launch, monitor, rollback) are being dry-run read-only against the cluster. A W&B report with both run sets over the trial window will be linked here before launch, along with each transition: forced checkpoint, cancel, launch, first steps, go/no-go.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This eval experiment tried to reproduce Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores on Marin for four large MoE baselines using Terminus 2, three attempts per task, a 250-turn limit, a 7,200-second agent timeout, and the pinned TB2.1 dataset. The main result is mixed. Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4 reproduced the AAII point estimate almost exactly at 54.09% versus 53.93%. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 was still preliminary in the posted table, at 42.34% versus 47.57% with 110/111 completed trials and 156 trials remaining. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 cleared the infrastructure-success gate but missed parity badly, scoring 56.23% versus AAII's 78.65% with no confirmed protocol discrepancy. GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4 produced no valid cohort because the checkpoint could not be served with the required context under the tested single-node geometry. The follow-up work is to finish Qwen, isolate the DeepSeek score gap, and rerun GLM with a serving geometry that preserves the intended context budget.

### Helpful links
- Experiment summary comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8261#issuecomment-5299403446
- Versioned launch configs and artifacts: https://huggingface.co/datasets/penfever/large-model-agentic-eval-parity-tb21-aa/tree/main/artifacts
- Baseline/context comment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8261#issuecomment-5299504940
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Human Authored tl;dr

WHAT THIS IS: The purpose of this experiment was to try to reproduce AAII tb2.1 eval scores on the Marin cluster on some strong baselines.
WHY WE DID IT: Exercise Marin's eval pipeline and thoroughly understand how AAII executes tb2.1, since minor differences in protocol can dramatically impact scores.
RESULT: Picked four models; Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4, GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4. GLM 5.2 did not run (needs either pipeline parallel or B200s or possibly both). Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4 succeeded. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 is slightly below parity but pretty close. DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is way below parity and there's no obvious discrepancy so I'm not sure why.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 ## Experiment summary

This experiment compares Marin's Terminal-Bench 2.1 results with the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (AAII) for four large MoE models. The protocol uses Terminus 2, three attempts per task (267 trials), a 250-turn limit, a 7,200-second agent timeout, and the pinned `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@sha256:7d7bdc1cbedad549fc1140404bd4dc45e5fd0ea7c4186773687d177ad3a0699a` dataset. Marin used Daytona sandboxes; AAII used E2B.

| Model | AAII | Marin | Delta | Scoreable trials | Infrastructure success | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B NVFP4 | 53.93% | 54.09% | +0.16 pp | 257/267 | 96.25% | Reproduced |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | 47.57% | 42.34% | -5.23 pp | 110/111 completed | 99.10% | Preliminary; 156 trials remain |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | 78.65% | 56.23% | -22.42 pp | 265/267 | 99.25% | Valid Marin result; parity failed |
| GLM-5.2 AWQ INT4 | 77.90% | — | — | 0/267 | 0.00% | No valid cohort |

The Qwen rerun aligns the 262,144-token serving context and 81,920-token generation limit across vLLM and Terminus 2. Its current 42.34% mean comprises 48 successes and 62 zeros. Thirteen `AgentTimeoutError` trials received verifier scores and are valid; one `VerifierTimeoutError` is an infrastructure failure.

Nemotron reproduces the AAII point estimate within 0.16 percentage points. DeepSeek clears the 90% infrastructure gate but remains 22.42 points below AAII with no confirmed protocol discrepancy. GLM did not produce a valid result because the AWQ checkpoint could not be served with the required context under the tested single-node geometry; pipeline parallelism or B200 capacity remains to be tested.

Checkpoint and environment differences limit the comparison. AAII evaluated unquantized Qwen and GLM checkpoints and BF16 Nemotron, while Marin used Qwen FP8, GLM AWQ INT4, and Nemotron NVFP4. DeepSeek used the same checkpoint family. The sandbox provider also differs.

Next steps are to finish the Qwen cohort, isolate the DeepSeek score gap, and rerun GLM with a serving geometry that preserves the intended context budget.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
One pod whose container exec fails in the runtime makes every Iris controller control tick raise. While that pod stays in that state, the controller dispatches and cleans up nothing.

On cw-rno2a, no task attempt has reached RUNNING in the controller database since 2026-11-06 21:59 UTC. 80 tasks across 8 users sit in `TASK_STATE_ASSIGNED`. Their pods can exist and run, because `sync` applies new pods before the polling step that raises. The controller never records them as running, so jobs that wait on a child's terminal state stall. The `marin` and `cw-us-east-02a` clusters are unaffected. The controller (build `260d937671`) logs this on every tick:

```
iris.cluster.controller.controller Control tick failed
  controller.py:1087 _control_tick -> self.backend.reconcile(...)
  backends/k8s/tasks.py:2658 sync -> self._poll_pods(...)
  backends/k8s/tasks.py:3278 _poll_pods -> self._finalize_task_outputs(entry, pod_name, pod)
  backends/k8s/tasks.py:3173 _finalize_task_outputs -> self.kubectl.exec(pod_name, ["touch", OUTPUT_RELEASE_PATH], ...)
  platforms/k8s/service.py:760 exec -> ExecResult(returncode=resp.returncode, ...)
  kubernetes/stream/ws_client.py:292 returncode -> int(err['details']['causes'][0]['message'])
ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'Internal error occurred: error executing command in container: failed to exec in container: failed to start exec "f3d16a5d…": OCI runtime exec f…'
```

When the runtime cannot start the exec, kubernetes-client 36.0.3 parses a non-numeric failure cause as the exit code. `CloudK8sService.exec` catches only `ApiException` and `TransportError`, and `_finalize_task_outputs` catches only `KubectlError`. The `ValueError` therefore escapes `sync`, `reconcile` and `_control_tick`, and the tick never commits. The same code is on current `main`.

Reproduce (unit level): call `CloudK8sService.exec` with a closed exec stream whose `returncode` is `kubernetes.stream.ws_client.WSClient.returncode`, and whose error channel returns `{"status": "Failure", "details": {"causes": [{"message": "Internal error occurred: ... OCI runtime exec failed"}]}}`. It raises `ValueError` instead of returning a failed `ExecResult`. Live: submit any job to cw-rno2a, for example `iris --cluster=cw-rno2a job run --cpu 0.1 --memory 256MB -- echo ok`. It stays ASSIGNED in the controller database. `iris rpc controller get-kubernetes-cluster-status` is not reliable here: its pod cache refreshes inside the failing tick, so it is stale.

No test covers this. `test_cloud_k8s_service.py` fakes exec streams only with integer return codes, and no provider or controller test asserts that one pod's unexpected error leaves the rest of `sync` and the tick intact.

Expected: an exec that cannot start returns a failed `ExecResult` (or a `KubectlError`), and one pod's failure in `_poll_pods` cannot abort reconcile for the whole cluster. Tests cover both.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 ## Research

`CloudK8sService.exec` reads the Kubernetes websocket's `returncode`, whose client parser raises `ValueError` when the runtime reports an OCI exec failure as a nonnumeric cause. `_finalize_task_outputs` catches only `KubectlError`, so that exception escapes pod polling and aborts the controller tick.

Relevant code:
- [`service.py#L760`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33748734802cbb9839a99731260bcc1977e1530e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/service.py#L760): reads the websocket exit code.
- [`tasks.py#L3179`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33748734802cbb9839a99731260bcc1977e1530e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L3179): releases the output uploader.
- [`tasks.py#L3285`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/33748734802cbb9839a99731260bcc1977e1530e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L3285): calls finalization during pod polling.

## Proposed Fix

Return a failed `ExecResult` when the websocket exit code is malformed. Keep output release failures local to that pod so polling can process other tasks, and add regressions for both boundaries.

```

```

Reproduce:
1. Run a verified copy of a multi-GB safetensors repository from Hugging Face to `s3://marin-rno2a/...`.
2. Staging and SHA-256 verification complete.
3. Promotion copies each shard with `cp_file(..., preserve_etag=True)` (`lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py:413`). The ETag recheck at `verified_copy.py:420-422` fails, and the promoted object is deleted.

| `marianna13/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-SFT-mix-v4-think-step465` @ `b4558699` | 00007 of 39 |

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
`fsutil verified-copy` into a CoreWeave S3 bucket cannot finish for any object stored as a multipart upload. The promote step fails with:

```
Error: promoted object does not match verified staging object: model-00001-of-00502.safetensors
```

This is current main: `lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py` was last changed in e9d42161ab ([#9606](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9606)).

## Cause

`_promote` copies the staged object with `filesystem.cp_file(staging_path, destination_path, preserve_etag=True)`. It then accepts the result only if the new ETag equals the staging ETag recorded in the resume marker (`_destination_matches_marker`, `staging_identity="etag=..."`). s3fs's `preserve_etag` path (`_copy_etag_preserved`) rebuilds the same part layout with `upload_part_copy`.

CoreWeave AI Object Storage gives a multipart object assembled from `UploadPartCopy` parts a different ETag than the same bytes uploaded with `UploadPart`, even when the part sizes are identical. The comparison can never succeed for multipart objects there. Single-part objects keep a plain MD5 ETag and promote fine.

Minimal reproduction against `s3://marin-rno2a` (rigging `filesystem_for`, s3fs 2026.1.0):

| Object (3 parts of 8 MiB + 1 MiB tail, random bytes) | ETag |
|---|---|
| Standard multipart ETag (md5 of part md5s) | `288f9995ba2170a993a398f1a1fcf144-3` |
| After upload (`open(..., "wb", block_size=8 MiB)`) | `288f9995ba2170a993a398f1a1fcf144-3` (matches) |
| After `cp_file(src, dst, preserve_etag=True)` | `55c8602f25d3f874ad13931d9b01d75d-3` (different; bytes identical) |

`head_object(PartNumber=i)` returns correct per-part ranges on CoreWeave: `bytes 0-52428799/656670848`, ..., part 13 `27525248` bytes. So s3fs reproduces the part layout correctly. Only the ETag differs.

## Observed

The copy was `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/rsi-merge/merges/avg-SC/` → `s3://marin-rno2a/scratch/karan/task289/merges/avg-SC/`, 509 objects, 134 GB, run as Iris jobs `/karan/rsi289-copy-avg-SC` and `/karan/rsi289-copy-avg-SC-r2` (2026-10-24).

- 429 objects promoted. 80 were left in `avg-SC.verified-copy-staging/`. The manifest has exactly 80 objects over the 50 MiB part size, which are the multipart ones.
- Example: `model-00001-of-00502.safetensors`, 656,670,848 bytes. Marker `staging_identity` was `etag=d635d51ef0ed17b23e7a1a0190357b4c-13`; the copied object's ETag was `7217d670f6e2dc4b0cdd681b1dbf9d1e-13`. The sha256 of the copy matches the source.
- The second merge (`ta-S-C-A5`, job `/karan/rsi289-copy-ta-S-C-A5`) shows the same pattern.

## Related: a failed upload leaves a committed partial object in staging

Both copies also died once on `OSError: [Errno 5] An error occurred (408) when calling the UploadPart operation: Request Timeout` (16 workers; 8 workers also hit it). `_copy_with_hash` writes inside `with destination_fs.open(staging_path, "wb", block_size=50 MiB)`. fsspec's `AbstractBufferedFile.__exit__` always calls `close()` → `flush(force=True)`, so s3fs completes the multipart upload with the parts already sent, even while an exception is propagating.

For `ta-S-C-A5`, `model-00140-of-00502.safetensors` and `model-00141-of-00502.safetensors` were left in staging at 209,715,200 bytes each (exactly 4 × 50 MiB) of 1,677,721,760.

verified-copy itself is safe here: no resume marker is written for those objects, and a rerun recopies them. But the staging prefix holds complete-looking objects that are truncated. Anything that reads staging directly gets bad data. A manual finishing step did this, and only a sha256 check against the source manifest caught it.

## Suggested fixes

1. In `_promote` (and in `_destination_matches_marker`), don't rely on ETag equality across a server-side copy for multipart objects. Either:
   - re-hash the promoted object with sha256 when the identity is a multipart ETag (`-N` suffix), or
   - for S3 backends, skip promote and write the final object directly, verifying sha256 on the destination as staging already does.
   Recording `sha256=` instead of `etag=` as the staging identity for multipart objects would also work.
2. In `_copy_with_hash`, abort the upload on error instead of committing it: call `destination.discard()` (s3fs aborts the MPU), or open with `autocommit=False` and `commit()` only after the loop completes. Then a failed copy leaves no object behind.
3. Consider retrying `UploadPart` 408s (`retries` in the s3fs client config). Two 134 GB copies each failed once at 8-16 workers.

## Workaround used

Finish the move in-cluster, then check every object's sha256 and size against the merge's own manifest. Script: `experiments/weight_merging/rsi/screen_289/finish_copy.py` on branch `task/289`. Delete truncated staged objects first and recopy them from the source.

comments.body:
🤖 **Research**

`_promote` requires the copied object's ETag to equal the staging ETag. CoreWeave changes multipart ETags for `UploadPartCopy`, so matching bytes fail promotion. A write error also exits the buffered writer through `close()`, which can complete a truncated multipart upload.

**Relevant code**
- [`verified_copy.py#L413-L421`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py#L413-L421) — promotion and identity check.

issues.title: [rigging] fsutil verified-copy cannot promote multipart objects on CoreWeave S3; failed uploads leave truncated staging objects

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Simplify `fsutil` verified copy so that it writes each file straight to its final path, with no staging prefix, no server-side promotion copy and no ETag recheck after promotion.

Today, `verified_copy_prefix` (`lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py`) works in three steps:
1. It uploads each file to a `.verified-copy-staging/` prefix while hashing the source stream.
2. It promotes the file with `cp_file(..., preserve_etag=True)` (`verified_copy.py:413`).
3. It accepts the promoted object only if its ETag matches the staging ETag (`verified_copy.py:420-422`).

CoreWeave gives a server-side copy a different multipart ETag for identical bytes, so promotion fails for every multipart object (#10638). #10639 works around that by reading back and re-hashing each promoted object whose ETag changed. That is correct, but on CoreWeave it re-reads every multipart file and writes every byte twice. Today's 125 GB model mirrors failed after about 45 minutes each, before the read-back would even have started.

Proposed design:
- **Write directly to the destination.** Upload each file as one multipart upload with autocommit off, hashing the source stream (SHA-256 and the expected multipart ETag) as it goes.
- **Complete only on a verified stream.** Call `CompleteMultipartUpload` only after the whole source has streamed without error and its size matches. When the source publishes a hash (the Hugging Face LFS sha256, or a GCS md5/crc32c), the streamed hash must also match it. Otherwise, abort the upload.
  - S3 publishes a multipart object atomically on completion, so a partial object is never visible at the final path.
- **Check the completed object** against the locally computed multipart ETag. Direct uploads use a fixed part size, so their ETag is predictable without a read-back.
- **Mark completion with the manifest.** The completion manifest is the only "copy done" marker, and readers check for it. Resume skips files whose destination size and ETag match their per-file record, and redoes the rest. Uploads still in progress at a crash are aborted and restarted rather than resumed part by part.
- **Other destinations.** GCS and local destinations get the same contract through their own atomic finalize: a GCS resumable upload, or a local write followed by a rename.

Prerequisite: #10639 merged. Keep its abort-on-failed-`UploadPart` fix, which this design subsumes. Once direct writes land, remove its post-promotion read-back.

Done when:
- A verified copy of a 39-shard, multi-GB safetensors repository from Hugging Face to `s3://marin-rno2a` completes, and its manifest records a SHA-256 per file. Each sha256 matches Hugging Face's LFS sha256.
- No staging prefix, server-side copy or post-upload read-back remains in the S3 path. Each destination byte is written once.
- A copy killed mid-file resumes without republishing completed files, and leaves no visible partial object or orphaned multipart upload.
- A forced mid-stream `UploadPart` failure aborts the upload and leaves no object at the destination path.
- The same tests pass for GCS and local destinations.

- [`verified_copy.py#L153-L259`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da4bba85a4b9ae57902bd26d00d700d9921398c7/lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py#L153-L259) — staging and promotion phases.
- [`verified_copy.py#L301-L365`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da4bba85a4b9ae57902bd26d00d700d9921398c7/lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py#L301-L365) — resume marker and source checks.
- [`verified_copy.py#L377-L477`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da4bba85a4b9ae57902bd26d00d700d9921398c7/lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py#L377-L477) — copy, ETag, and read-back paths.
- [`verified_copy.py#L613-L642`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da4bba85a4b9ae57902bd26d00d700d9921398c7/lib/rigging/src/rigging/fsutil/verified_copy.py#L613-L642) — source and destination identities.

# Direct destination copy plan

Keep the `verified_copy_prefix` API and completion-manifest format. Start from #10639 after it merges, then remove the staging location, `_promote`, and the post-promotion SHA-256 read-back. Files may appear at their final paths before the manifest; readers of a verified prefix must require `.verified-copy-manifest.json` before treating the prefix as complete.

Capture an advertised source checksum separately from its version/change token. Resolve Hugging Face LFS SHA-256 and GCS MD5 or CRC32C from their source metadata, compare them with hashes computed while streaming, and reject a mismatch before publication. Continue recording SHA-256 for every file in the manifest even when a source publishes no checksum.

For S3, open the final key with fixed parts and `autocommit=False`. Check streamed size, any advertised checksum, and the source's post-stream identity before `commit()`; discard on source, hash, or `UploadPart` failure. After commit, HEAD the key and compare size and the locally computed ETag, including the one-part MPU case. Delete a committed key on verification failure. Write a per-file status record containing the final object's identity only after that check; publish the manifest last. On restart, reuse a file only when its source token, destination size, and destination identity match the record; otherwise overwrite it. Old staging records cannot authorize reuse and should be discarded after successful completion.

A process killed mid-upload cannot run `discard()`. Persist enough S3 upload ownership information to abort this transfer's unfinished MPU IDs on restart, without touching uploads from another writer; use explicit multipart calls if s3fs cannot expose those IDs. For GCS, confirm that its resumable writer keeps an object invisible until successful finalize; for local files, write a sibling temp file and rename after validation. Apply the same per-file resume and manifest rules to both backends.

**Validation:** Add behavior tests for source checksum and size mismatches, one- and multi-part ETag checks, failed `UploadPart`, kill-and-resume, stale destination records, and GCS/local finalize failures. Check that failure leaves no manifest, visible partial file, or orphaned MPU, and that resume does not republish a verified file. After a small live CoreWeave probe, run the issue's 39-shard Hugging Face copy to `s3://marin-rno2a`; compare every manifest SHA-256 with the LFS SHA-256 and confirm no staging copy or destination read-back occurs.

**Open questions:** Confirm the metadata path for LFS SHA-256 in the configured Hugging Face filesystem, and identify every consumer that must gate reads on the manifest. The current copy API publishes a manifest but does not enforce that rule for external readers.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
The pinned Micro210 release cannot run its `tau3-pi` task through current Harbor backends without changing the task's environment contract. This blocks the long-loop SFT → RL → evaluation smoke.

Reproduce on Marin main `1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0`:

1. Read `data/validation.parquet` from [open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Micro-Eval-210/tree/4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819), revision `4564ed081c316bc3231ae5c3a53a46b39248c819`.
2. Restore a `tau3-pi` task with `skyrl_train.dataset.harbor_import.restore_harbor_trial_task`. The release uses TaskSpec 0.28; decode it with the release schema or explicitly convert its script/Harbor task fields to 0.30 first.
3. Construct a Harbor `Trial` with the restored task, `AgentConfig(name="pi")`, and a Daytona environment with explicit host capabilities. The task has two Compose services: `main` and `tau3-runtime`.
4. Repeat with the local environment backend.

Daytona rejects construction with `Shellbox Daytona supports single-container tasks; use local for Compose service groups` ([check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/daytona.py#L132)). Local rejects the task's existing `allow_internet=true` setting with `Prepared service groups require allow_internet=false` ([check](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker_translate.py#L246)). These are local constructor errors before provider calls; changing Daytona organizations does not resolve them.

Done when:

- The pinned task has a supported, tested backend preserving its two-service topology, health-check ordering, shared agent-log mount, and model access through a host relay. Any change to its declared network policy is explicit and justified against the original package.
- Construction preflight detects incompatible packages before a cluster launch.
- A tau3 end-to-end smoke completes and cleans up both services.

The experimental `experiments/post_training/long_loop/` smoke temporarily excludes `tau3-pi` and records reduced coverage. Restore it after the supported backend passes the smoke; do not report the reduced run as complete Micro210 coverage.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At main `1cf5c009`, Daytona rejects Compose packages, while Harbor's local translator rejects the release's `allow_internet=true` and assigns `NetworkPolicy.DENY` to every service. SkyRL also limits original Harbor trials to Daytona, so changing the translator alone cannot run this task. The existing local tau3-style test exercises service health ordering, a host model relay, log handoff, and cleanup with a synthetic `allow_internet=false` package; it does not establish support for the pinned Micro210 row.

**Relevant code**
- [`daytona.py#L132-L136`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/daytona.py#L132-L136) — rejects Compose
- [`docker_translate.py#L179-L183`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker_translate.py#L179-L183) and [`#L237-L246`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker_translate.py#L237-L246) — denies network and rejects the flag
- [`agent_runtime.py#L141-L160`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/agent_runtime.py#L141-L160) — requires Daytona
- [`launch.py#L80-L104`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/launch.py#L80-L104) — prepares task references before submission
- [`test_prepared_service_group.py#L87-L221`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1cf5c009d358261bd41f368bcd033197ecd731f0/vendor/harbor/tests/unit/environments/test_prepared_service_group.py#L87-L221) — synthetic local tau3 coverage

# Proposed Fix

Use Harbor's local prepared service-group backend for this Compose task, preserving the released `allow_internet=true` contract. Implement in these gates:

1. Decode the pinned `validation.parquet` row with its TaskSpec 0.28 schema or a tested explicit 0.28→0.30 conversion. Restore its original package and capture `task.toml`, Compose, image build inputs, MCP endpoint, and network requirements as a regression fixture. Do not silently change the package's network flag.
2. Prepare digest-pinned images and absolute workdirs for both `main` and `tau3-runtime`; provide the local backend's `shellbox-images.json` declaration, including sidecar agent-log publication. Make the Compose translator map the task's declared internet policy to each service's Shellbox network policy. Verify that the local backend can enforce `ALLOW` while retaining private service networking and the host model relay; if it cannot, stop at preflight and choose a backend that can, instead of rewriting the release.
3. Extend SkyRL's original-trial settings and harness to select Harbor local for this package and pass explicit host model capabilities without Daytona credentials. Keep the sidecar health check before the main agent, the MCP endpoint, shared agent-log handoff before verification, and cleanup of both services on success and failure.
4. At the long-loop launch boundary, validate each selected pinned package against the chosen backend before Iris submission: schema conversion, prepared images, Compose subset, network policy, model relay, and host requirements. Fail with the task ID and incompatible field. A constructor-only negative test must prove an invalid package cannot launch.
5. Run the pinned single-task local trial, then the SFT → RL → evaluation smoke. Record graded output and both-service cleanup. Restore `tau3-pi` to the experimental long-loop smoke only after that evidence exists; keep reduced coverage explicit until then.

The local `ALLOW` capability and preparation of the release's two images are the first feasibility checks. [#10817](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10817) records prior validation on a different runtime; it does not cover this current-main constructor failure. [#11080](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11080) changes nearby vendored Harbor code, so the implementation should be based on its resolved state.

issues.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Catalog source](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals)

**Living summary — updated October 22, 2026.** Detailed evidence is linked from each result.

### Current results

| Model / benchmark | Result | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snowball v0.1 Smartie Step14 / BixBench corrections v3 / Pi 1.3.0 | **19/205 (9.3%)**; all scored, only 48 nonempty submissions | [Result and reviewed trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) |
| Snowball v0.1 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **4.24/100**; 50/50 scored, 12/50 with any nonempty report (5/50 with both) | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-snowball-v01-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / BiomniBench-DA / Pi 0.87.0 / 60-minute protocol | **71.14/100**; 50/50 scored, 45/50 with both reports | [EvalDash](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/20261022-165801-glm-5.3-biomnibench-da-60min-full-b3c4) · [Comparison and audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649) |
| GLM-5.3 / MMLU biology | **462/554**; 81.79% mean subject accuracy, 83.39% pooled | [Run and subject results](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647) (Marina access) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench CLI v1.5 / Terminus-2 | **101/187 graded (54.01%)**; 18/205 ungraded | [Baseline and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Terminus-2 | **42/49 graded (85.71%)**; 1/50 ungraded; saved-answer regrade | [Regrade and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) |
| GLM-5.3 / BixBench-Verified-50 / Pi 0.87.0 | **39/46 graded (84.78%)**; 4/50 ungraded | [Run investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) |

Across benchmark rows, variants, agents, judges, budgets, and grading policies differ. The two BiomniBench-DA rows share the task/input preparation, Pi agent, rubric/judge and budget policy, with disclosed model-serving differences and reused early completions. BiomniBench-DA tasks with no nonempty report score zero; these scores are rubric-score means, not accuracy. Other GLM rows separately report ungraded outcomes.

### Current findings

Snowball’s BixBench failures are dominated by **156 missing answer files**, plus one empty submission. Traces show answers left in chat, simulated execution without real tool calls, repetition, and specific analysis mistakes. Compaction count showed little association with missing files. BFCL also had **55/123 missing submissions**; four inspected examples show related submission/tool-use failures beyond biology, without establishing one shared cause. No scores were changed.

The completed BiomniBench-DA comparison scores **Snowball 4.24/100 versus GLM-5.3 71.14/100**, with all 50 outcomes per model verified against native rewards, sealed archives and EvalDash rows. Snowball produced no nonempty report on 38/50 tasks; GLM did so on 5/50. All 38 selected Snowball cases ended normally within 24 minutes, so the separately confirmed Pi timeout leak cannot explain them. This supports a file-delivery/tool-use gap under these model-serving configurations; checkpoint versus tool/serving integration remains unresolved, and this does not establish a general biology knowledge deficit.

The 60-minute protocol retained 83 unaffected outcomes from the earlier 30-minute budget and reran deadline-affected tasks from scratch. It uses five disclosed input variants and a replacement MiniMax judge/signed rubric scorer, remains supplementary, and does not change the release aggregate. The continuation used the [Harbor timeout repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/3bc27cbcffad1d92ad5d9bd4c83cd3f36bf89372); an unresolved `/tokenize` HTTP 502 diagnostic affects interpretation of one GLM timeout. [Full comparison, launch-source references, audit and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6349556649).

[Selected HF traces](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/snowball-v01-bixbench-trace-examples) show recurring simulated execution, chat-only answers, and repetitive output-limit failures across BiomniBench-DA, BixBench, and BFCL. BiomniBench also has wrong-path and rejected-write examples. These support general execution/submission problems without establishing a shared cause; [the comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6297505720) records the examples and differing Pi versions.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 BixBench CLI development check: the explicit 10 GiB retry ran through the agent phase, but produced no scored answer. The initial attempt had been blocked before model inference because the task's default 20 GB disk request exceeded the Daytona account's 10 GB per-sandbox cap.

The retry used `environment.override_storage_mb: 10240`, following a [previous Harbor canary that hit the same limit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/75#issuecomment-5461786985). Development outcome:

- Sandbox setup completed. The agent ran for its original 3,600-second budget without creating `/workspace/answer.txt`.
- BixBench's unchanged verifier returns without writing a reward when the answer file is missing. Harbor recorded `RewardFileNotFoundError`; no Together judge decision was produced. The canonical record reports **1 attempted, 0 scored**. This is not a judged incorrect answer or a benchmark accuracy estimate.
- The end-of-agent filesystem diagnostic reported **25.7 MiB used and 9.97 GiB available** in the 10 GiB allocation. No disk-exhaustion failure was observed. This is a final filesystem reading, not peak usage or the base image's total size, and it does not establish that every capsule fits.

Protocol:

- CLI adaptation, registry `bixbench-cli@1.5`, [task revision `711ff277`](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-datasets/tree/711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73/datasets/bixbench-cli). One development task, `bix-1-q1`, excluded from the subsequent five-question pilot. The complete registry snapshot has 205 questions.

Use the [September evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9193): 32,768 input tokens, 8,192 output tokens, and the default enabled summarization.
- Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` verifier with BixBench's original grading prompt and Boolean response schema. Four basic live checks passed: exact and equivalent numeric answers accepted; wrong and empty answers rejected. This checks grader integration, not broad judge accuracy.
- The original base image is ARM-only. Use the [adapter author's AMD64 replacement](https://github.com/Future-House/BixBench/issues/41#issuecomment-4340332343), pinned to `sha256:485e5c776422fece8cb98addba593ea188c8a97162807a91d2a0e350522407b7`, with capsule data pinned to Hugging Face revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`.

The five-question pilot has not been launched. Before expanding, review the no-answer timeout behavior and complete a native verifier check that reaches the judge. The current failure remains in the record; it must not disappear from attempted coverage. This exploratory CLI protocol should be reported separately from the original notebook-based BixBench leaderboard and from Marin's canonical benchmark suite.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 The five-question GLM-5.3 BixBench CLI pilot completed with an answer from every task. The original verifier scored three answers: one correct, two incorrect, and two unscored because structured JSON generation exhausted the judge's token limit. The incomplete original run retains no aggregate metric.

A separate, uniform regrade of the same five saved answers added an explicit JSON-schema instruction to the judge. It produced one correct and four incorrect results, with no JSON errors; the three previously valid grades stayed unchanged. This is a five-question integration pilot with a disclosed judge-prompt variation, not a full-benchmark accuracy estimate. The original answers, trajectories, and scores were preserved.

The format repair is in [Harbor commit `97037f79`](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800). It preserves the comparison prompt, Boolean schema, judge model, and 1,024-token cap. Lint and formatting passed. The branch has no PR yet; existing registry snapshots still require regenerated or explicitly patched tasks.

Error review:

- `bix-11-q2`: 88/249 fungal trees exceed the treeness threshold, giving 35.34%, versus the reference's 35%. The regrader rejected the difference. This is a likely precision-related false negative; no score has been changed. The pinned question specifies no rounding rule, and its archive contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-52-q2`: the agent used pooled CpGs / genome length. The [reference capsule](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) groups only chromosomes containing retained CpGs (notebook cells 11 and 39). Averaging those 20 chromosome densities yields 1.1283e-7, inside the reference interval. The notebook confirms the chromosome selection; the mean was recomputed from the saved table.
- `bix-28-q1`: the final analysis substituted raw terminal branch lengths and species-level medians for the [PhyKIT long-branch statistic](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/reference/commands/long_branch_score.html). The reference p-value has not been independently reproduced; its archive also contains no reference notebook.
- `bix-6-q7`: the agent used a top-1% replicate intersection, then mistook its own intermediate enrichment CSV for supplied results. The [reference notebook](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-f4dcda89-678d-403d-b155-1483d0071765.zip), cells 28–30, instead takes the minimum replicate P-value, selects values below 0.05, maps RefSeq IDs to symbols, and runs Reactome enrichment against measured genes. It reports “cGMP effects” with raw P ≈ 0.000024 and adjusted P ≈ 0.0327. These are saved reference outputs, not a fresh rerun.
- `bix-18-q2`: the mean swarming area was correctly rounded to 82,000.

Six additional fixed judge diagnostics accepted `35.0%` as equivalent to `35%`, rejected `45%`, and classified one value inside and one outside the CpG reference interval correctly. The exact-percent and higher-precision examples returned provider server errors, so this check did not resolve the rounding concern. No tolerance or solver setting was retuned.

The [previously documented protocol](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5736346928) and explicit environment overrides were retained. All five pilot agents submitted within their original time limits, with no observed disk exhaustion. The full 205-question run remains pending a decision on numerical grading; original scores will remain intact.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 GLM-5.3 completed 205 fresh BixBench CLI attempts: **101 correct / 187 graded (54.01%)**, with **18 ungraded**. Grading coverage is **91.22%**. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is **43.79–63.43%**; 54.01% is the accuracy among graded questions.

All 177 valid native grades were retained. Eleven saved answers whose verifier calls failed with HTTP 503 received one additional grading attempt each, with the original SDK retry policy. Ten obtained grades (eight correct, two incorrect); one still failed with a provider error. No solver was rerun or answer edited. The original run and its artifacts remain preserved.

The 18 ungraded outcomes are:

- 14 missing answer/reward files following the 3,600-second agent limit.
- Two sandbox processes killed with exit 137 (`TmuxBatchProtocolError`); the cause is unconfirmed.
- One Daytona HTTP 502 gateway failure.
- One unresolved judge server error (`bix-10-q2`).

Three other trials reported `AgentTimeoutError` but produced valid verifier results; those grades remain included. Missing grades are excluded from the accuracy denominator and shown separately. The original private exporter mistakenly required 100% grading coverage; its incomplete record is preserved. The derived result applies [Marin's standard 90% completion gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/a28c29a008a3ddc1a62fb348c52217a4429e5491/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py), consistent with the reporting policy in #9193. The original sample export displayed missing rewards as incorrect; the derived archive preserves all 18 as ungraded.

Protocol: `bixbench-cli@1.5`, Harbor `7b18505a56e5624f55887e3b20f4de452f698a7a`, task revision `711ff277ae6b9e3950d19b40bc3e5aeb96e62b73`, Terminus-2, 16 concurrent trials, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, and 3,600-second agent / 600-second verifier limits. The judge was Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with the original comparison prompt and 1,024-token cap. The [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800) applied to every task; numerical tolerances were unchanged. The [previously documented](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5742640265) 10 GiB disk override, pinned AMD64 image, and task-manifest hash were retained.

Validation checked all 205 task identities, sample counts against aggregate scores, all retained native grades, and the eleven selected recovery cases. Two archived trajectories were also compared byte-for-byte through the dashboard API. This establishes an exploratory CLI baseline; ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The replacement judge, missing grades, known precision caveat from the pilot, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons with other protocols. Next: review full-run scientific errors and compare future models under this same recorded protocol.

comments.author: gonzalobenegas
comments.body:
🤖 Reviewed all 86 recorded incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes from the [completed BixBench CLI baseline](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667), using saved answers/trajectories and the archived reference notebooks where available. No solver or judge calls were rerun. The result remains **101/187 correct (54.01%), with 18/205 ungraded**.

Each incorrect answer has a primary review category:

| Category | Questions | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Observed analysis or protocol divergence | 54 | Identified differences in statistic, counting unit, filtering, cohort, model or enrichment workflow. Some choices are underspecified in the question; these are not all established scientific mistakes. |
| Answer precision or representation review | 11 | Submitted values may differ through rounding or units; this does not establish 11 false negatives. |
| Question or reference adjudication | 7 | Contradictory targets, unclear counting/aggregation, or unresolved reference-data provenance. |
| Numerical or pipeline mismatch unresolved | 14 | Insufficient evidence to isolate the cause without reconstructing more of the reference pipeline. |

The review ledger records a finding, confidence level, trace evidence and pinned reference capsule for each of the 104 nonpassing outcomes. Original trajectories remain in the existing evaluation archive; the detailed review ledger is retained with the private evaluation handoff. The categories above are follow-up queues, not a corrected accuracy estimate.

Concrete analysis findings:

- `bix-61-q1`: reported **4,818 discarded read pairs across two samples**. The MDR trimming log reconstructs the reference's **344,895 discarded individual reads** exactly: 334,988 forward-only survivors + 1,075 reverse-only survivors + 2 × 4,416 fully dropped pairs. Both the counting unit and sample scope changed.
- `bix-28-q4` and `bix-45-q5`: substituted a different statistic. The former used terminal-branch means grouped by species instead of per-tree long-branch scores; the latter used BUSCO score/cutoff instead of [PhyKIT relative composition variability](https://jlsteenwyk.com/PhyKIT/tutorials/pages/01-summarizing-information-content.html).
- `bix-16-q1/q3`: raw Chronos scores were used without the reference's sign reversal. `bix-20-q1/q3`: unclassified variants entered the denominator; the reference excludes them, giving 13/14 and 35/37. These differences are visible in the [essentiality reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-bda54b38-9b49-4009-aad6-d5f52675438a.zip), cell 34, and [variant reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-2ccdbe37-0a92-47b5-9bab-fa8a8c470799.zip), cell 18.
- RNA-seq failures repeatedly differed in count normalization, outlier exclusion, covariates, nominal versus adjusted p-values, enrichment gene lists and background. For example, the [JBX13 reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-1d54e4a7-8b0f-4224-bd31-efcfded0d46c.zip) removes three samples and models replicate, strain and medium; several answers retained all samples and omitted replicate. The [UBE2M reference](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) removes KL3/WL3 before enrichment, unlike the `bix-53-q6` answer. Exact contributions were not isolated through reruns.
- `bix-10` / `bix-29` severity questions also expose a reference-definition caveat: the [reference preprocessing](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-fbe0e950-76f2-4eb7-a216-a2d377970922.zip), cell 17, aggregates all adverse events per participant, although questions call the endpoint COVID severity. COVID-specific/event-level alternatives therefore need protocol adjudication.

Grading and reference findings:

- `bix-19-q2` is a calculation-versus-submission example: the agent computed **Cohen's d = 0.216284**, independently matching [reference cell 30](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-8c64b1fa-fdcc-41e2-be8d-2f0c8d5faaa1.zip), but submitted approximately **0.22**. That final answer falls outside the target interval **0.215–0.217**. Other precision candidates include 35.34% versus 35% and 5.23 versus 5.2. The 11 cases are `4-q1/q5/q6`, `11-q1/q2/q5`, `19-q2`, `28-q6`, `38-q1/q3`, and `54-q5`, all with prefix `bix-`. Tiny nonzero p-values are not automatically equivalent to literal zero; `54-q5` also has a model-input difference alongside its ratio/fraction representation.
- `bix-53-q4` has a confirmed malformed target: the question requests a **pathway count**, but the [original ideal answer](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/BixBench.jsonl) is **4.25E-04**. [Reference cell 79](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) explicitly counts **2** pathways. The submitted answer was **1**, so fixing the target would not automatically make it correct.
- `bix-31-q2` contradicts its stated analysis. The target interval **−0.45 to −0.35** conflicts with **abs(LFC)>0.5**. [Reference cells 32–38](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) show FAM138A at baseMean **0.483698**, unshrunk LFC **−0.383938**, and shrunk LFC **−0.060666**. The target matches the unshrunk, low-expression row despite instructions requiring shrinkage and baseMean>10. The agent answered `NA`.
- `bix-52-q1` has a reference-data bug: [reference cell 14](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) downloads **JD_Chromosome_Length.csv** into **ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv**. The agent's **1.52** ratio is internally consistent with the supplied lengths and site counts; the provenance of the target **0.47–0.67** remains unresolved. `bix-52-q5` also counts repeated records instead of distinct sites, so this data caveat does not explain all CpG failures.
- The remaining four primary adjudication cases are `bix-8-q6` (260 unique genes versus 680 transcript records; [reference cell 21](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-48a6b469-9c9d-4bef-b5b4-f29b7d6fa046.zip) counts rows), `bix-38-q6` (median of paired ratios versus ratio of group medians), `bix-43-q4` (8/514 DE genes versus 8/49 pathway genes), and `bix-22-q6` (the origin of the 0.3–0.4 correlation target was not established). These require explicit definitions or reference reconstruction.
- `bix-54-q4` additionally has reversed target interval bounds, but its submitted p-value lies outside even the sorted interval. This metadata defect does not rescue that answer.

The [verifier](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800/adapters/bixbench/src/bixbench/task-template/tests/llm_judge.py) asks an LLM for binary equivalence. It has **no separate global numerical-tolerance rule**; some targets contain explicit intervals. The JSON-schema repair changes response format, not this comparison prompt. Before any rescoring, define a consistent precision/adjudication policy and preserve the present native grades as a separate baseline.

The 14 missing-answer traces show long model fits, repeated workbook inspection, unresolved analysis choices, and sensitivity checks after intermediate results existed. More time alone is not a demonstrated fix. The two exit-137 cases show killed statistical processes; excessive worker creation is a plausible contributor, but an OOM cause is unconfirmed. One gateway failure and `bix-10-q2`'s persistent judge 503 remain ungraded. The latter has a saved answer outside its target interval, but no manual grade was substituted.

Next: adjudicate the flagged question/reference and precision cases; document the intended analysis protocols; then select a small set of failures for any separately approved controlled rerun. Keep any revised scoring or solver results separate from this baseline. The existing verifier JSON-format PR follow-up remains open.

Reference links above use dataset revision `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; notebook cell indices are zero-based. Several phylogenetic and genomic-pipeline capsules contain no reference notebook, which limits causal conclusions for the 14 unresolved cases.

🤖 Agent-runtime summary for the [completed 205-question BixBench CLI run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667). Measured from each original Harbor trial’s `agent_execution.started_at` and `finished_at`; all 205 have both timestamps.

The median agent runtime was **5.6 minutes per question**. The middle 50% took **1.7–15.5 minutes**, and the 90th percentile was **37.3 minutes**.

| Questions | n | Median, min | 25th–75th percentile, min | 90th percentile, min | Mean, min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All attempted questions | 205 | 5.6 | 1.7–15.5 | 37.3 | 12.8 |
| Solver completed without interruption | 185 | 4.7 | 1.6–13.8 | 20.5 | 8.6 |
| Final grade: correct | 101 | 2.3 | 0.9–9.2 | 17.3 | 6.9 |
| Final grade: incorrect | 86 | 8.1 | 2.8–14.8 | 26.5 | 12.3 |

These are elapsed solving times, including model responses, command execution, waits and tool/network latency during the agent phase. They exclude separately timed sandbox setup, agent setup and grading. Quantiles use linear interpolation at `(n−1)×p`.

**17/205 tasks (8.3%) reached the configured 3,600-second agent cap**: 14 had no submitted answer and remained ungraded; 3 retained gradeable answers. The other three interrupted agents had two process-kill failures and one gateway failure. Capped times measure time spent before termination, not the uncensored time required to solve those tasks. Recorded capped durations were 3,600.0–3,602.3 seconds.

The median complete trial duration, including setup, grading and teardown, was **7.3 minutes**. The interval from the first trial start to the last trial finish was **3 h 28 min 48 s**.

The 185 uninterrupted solver completions include one answer whose judge still failed. Correct/incorrect rows use final saved-answer recovery grades and retain the three scored timeouts. Runtime differences between outcome groups are descriptive; task difficulty and workflow differences confound interpretation.

The complete launcher-to-export span was **3 h 36 min 11 s**, with a cap of **16 concurrent trials**. That batch span includes setup and final export; later saved-answer judge recovery is excluded. The [existing result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) remains 101/187 correct with 18 ungraded.

Per-question times, raw timestamps, source hashes and the summary calculation are retained in the private evaluation handoff. No new evaluation or grading calls were made.

No original reference notebook was available for this capsule. | Ask for a nonzero reference p-value with documented test options, or an explicit threshold/rounding instruction. A factor-of-ten typo is plausible but not established, and the agent and notebook use different cohorts. |

| [bix-31-q2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-b1dbace7-f6e9-42ec-81e1-bcc24161cc27.zip) | NA → Between -0.45 and -0.35 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The capsule annotation identifies FAM138A as lncRNA. Notebook cell 26 fits batch + sex; cell 32 gives baseMean 0.483698 and unshrunk LFC -0.383938; cell 36 gives shrunk LFC -0.060666. The target -0.45 to -0.35 matches the unshrunk row, contradicting the protein-coding, baseMean >10, abs(LFC)>0.5 and shrinkage requirements. Independent Newick branch-length sums find 96 paired orthologs and median(fungal_length/animal_length) = 1.9036165971, matching the submission. The target 2.178 instead matches the ratio of separately rounded group medians, 3.0962/1.4219 = 2.1775089669; that uses all 249 fungal and 100 animal trees. Full-precision group medians give 2.177433, also a different estimand. | Keep the paired-ratio question; reference 1.9036165971 with a declared tolerance, or explicitly request 1.904 to three decimal places. Preserve the paired ortholog list and full-precision input calculation. |

The prompt asks for the proportion of differentially expressed genes, but reference cell 65 reports the Enrichr overlap 8/49, whose denominator is pathway members. If retaining the DEG-proportion wording, establish mapping/deduplication and recompute that denominator. Do not certify 514 as the reference count. |
| [bix-52-q1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-4dceea58-7d66-4576-bfc6-88c026d5b7a9.zip) | Chromosome W / chromosome 1 = 1.52 → Between 0.47 and 0.67 inclusive | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. Packaged ZF_Chromosome_Length.csv is byte-identical to JD_Chromosome_Length.csv (SHA256 59e321ef…051b); notebook cell 14 downloads the JD file under the ZF name. | [bix-53-q4](https://huggingface.co/datasets/futurehouse/BixBench/blob/f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a/CapsuleFolder-308d53bf-1513-4a09-913b-3a1112f94e7b.zip) | 1 → 4.25E-04 | **Confirmed task/reference defect**. The submitted one is not correct merely because the gold is malformed. | Use integer target 2 only with the notebook's intended cohort, adjusted-p filtering, shrinkage and pathway-term matching explicitly specified. The current question says p while the notebook filters padj; pin that distinction before a corrected task is released. |

Reference cells 16/19 use rhlI/(rhlI+lasI) and yield a spline maximum at 0.9076577. The prompt asks for a ratio but the target stores a fraction. The agent selected the best tested ratio from 36 mixed-culture rows; the reference spline used 39 rows, so final-answer equivalence does not validate the method. | State that the answer is the rhlI fraction; allow an explicitly labeled equivalent mixture ratio if retaining outcome-only grading. Keep the method caveat separate. |

Evidence uses the pinned BixBench dataset `f8cc3bdcc6357c88b8c3648306522b9c422dc95a`; task links above point to the corresponding source capsule. Notebook cell numbers are zero-based. Local reproduction records include the downloaded-member SHA256 manifest, gene/correlation checks, and all 96 paired tree ratios. The corrected Zebra Finch file is available in [the original Zenodo dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/12205202).

A separate [public BixBench audit](https://github.com/Anqi-Dai/BixBench_eval/blob/6070dc293677b0ef21fa38d7ab23c5850d8799c0/env/REVIEW_REPORT.md) independently documents the 680-record/260-gene mismatch. Its study covers three capsules and fourteen questions; it does not validate this entire run.

The proposed precision rule was also screened against **all 205 saved outcomes, including the 101 previously correct answers**. This was a conservative scalar/range screen, not a complete semantic regrade: 81 answers require semantic parsing, and counts, unit conversions, reversed ranges and the zero p-value need explicit treatment. It flags two existing passes that a naive comparator would reject: `bix-18-q5` supplies 0.29 against a percent-scale 25–30 target, and `bix-45-q1` supplies 7.70e-54 against 7.6968e-54. The latter needs symmetric handling of reported precision, rather than always requiring the target's extra digits. These findings block adopting a blanket rounding rule or publishing a selectively corrected accuracy.

Harbor Index provides relevant prior work: its public index includes five BixBench-derived tasks, with eighteen trials each. [Its Jackdaw notes](https://hub.harborframework.com/tasks/harbor-index/bix-cpg-density-jackdaw/latest) explicitly say the scientific derivation was not re-audited. Later [PR #142](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) fixed underspecified instructions for two tasks present in this run: miRNA analysis `bix-30-q1` ([issue #97](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/97)) and ordinal regression `bix-10-q2` ([issue #113](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/issues/113)). The fixes specify preprocessing/modeling choices while retaining the targets. These are useful precedents for task repair, not grounds for changing our recorded grades. The index uses its own 1,200-second budgets and deterministic numeric verifiers; its results are not directly comparable to this baseline.

Next: review the seven local upstream-report drafts; agree on versioned task repairs and numerical tolerances; then validate any revised grader across all 205 outcomes before publishing a separate result. The fourteen other numerical/pipeline discrepancies and ungraded outcomes remain follow-ups. The main issue table records **per-question agent time**, with no total-duration column.

🤖 The pilot is idle with no GPU jobs running. Both planned 10-step attempts stopped in tiny-model preflight before student loading. Working Snowball SFT precedents now include a report on the same September 21 checkpoint, but the exact training path is not yet matched to this pilot. Resume after obtaining a reproducible working revision/configuration and reviewing the remaining differences. The baseline remains 0/1; the earlier four-step model’s incoherent evaluation remains ungraded.

<details>
<summary>Checkpoint, smoke findings, and next steps (September 23, 2026)</summary>

- **Hold further GPU runs; closer precedent identified (September 23):** The user supplied the text of [Harshit Varma’s report](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1374989195109466122/1552425627976474645). It continues the same `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` checkpoint on filtered AgentTrove plus GLM-5.3 RST successes: 63,504 rows, two epochs/722 steps, batch 64, sequence 32,768, `5e-5` AdamH with cosine and 3% warmup. Reported held-out NLL improves 1.094 → 0.909 and parse-fail turns fall 67% → 25%, while premature completion, recovery, and long-context behavior regress. This supports a functioning SFT/serving path for our student, not a claim of improved overall TB2 performance. The screenshot does not give hardware, code revision, or the exact optimizer class.

  The completed four-step biology pilot used ordinary Adam at constant `5e-5`; the unexecuted ten-step plan uses ordinary Adam with cosine and no warmup. GLM-5.3 then passed all 32 numerical checks, with one attempt per instance, no trial retries, and no summarization. Collection used [Harbor@17c0f88](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/17c0f88be98b357c0c27bbf7d7e5fd6e3e6b4e8a). Results: [first teacher attempt](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/bio-siblings-glm53-smoke-20260922-160257-teacher), [remaining 31](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/bio-siblings-glm53-batch31-20260922-161619-teacher). This observed reward shortcut must be addressed before using this family for RL.

The rendered corpus has 87,442 tokens and 26,963 assistant tokens. The native loader adds one BOS per conversation, giving 87,473 input tokens; assistant-only loss masks remain unchanged. CPU validation passed for all 31 conversations with a 4,096-token limit, no packing, and no validation split. The longest conversation is 3,477 tokens. The batch run's `results/training-corpus/` contains `manifest.json`, the complete 32-attempt ledger, method-review decisions, native conversations, Harmony records, rendered text, and the audit source. The prepared next evaluation pins [Harbor@d072bef](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/tree/d072bef08e54050880b484eb81d892944d1d82fb), including [bounded summary fallbacks](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/193), and explicitly sets `llm_call_kwargs.max_tokens=8192`, consistent with [Marin #9327](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9327). The original task bytes and student revision are unchanged. Before/after runs will use the same pinned training chat template without forcing a thinking prefix; the earlier default-thinking smoke is preserved separately.
- Eight-GPU investigation: two optimizer updates completed on the full 67B architecture with initialized weights and synthetic tokens. Configuration: [PR #9316 at `9394f2c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9394f2cd2b6c1b2154dd26c69e230df715fcaf99), 8×H100 80GB, 64 CPU cores / 768 GiB host RAM, one JAX process, BF16 parameters, demo MuonH/Adam optimizer, optimizer-state host offloading, context sharding across 8 devices, batch 8, sequence length 4,096, and `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.9`. Execution took 218.9 seconds and peak JAX allocator use was 67,653,347,256 bytes (63.01 GiB) per GPU. This excludes allocations outside JAX and does not establish checkpoint-specific SFT quality. No pretrained weights were downloaded and no checkpoints were written. The GPUs are released. The existing small-model HF import/logit and shared-expert checkpoint tests also passed on CPUs. The full pinned checkpoint import/export and actual-trace training remain to be validated. No expert-freezing or LoRA method has been adopted.

The generator source matches the original task-manifest hashes. CPU job `/exedev/bio-grug-data-preflight-20260922-184716` succeeded against the candidate training backend: all 31 conversations retained exact assistant-only loss weights over 256 presentations (8 or 9 per conversation, 222,695 supervised tokens), with no packing or validation split. The GPU probe used synthetic tokens; a pretrained run with these conversations remains pending.

The run was stopped after 642 seconds, before the configured one-hour agent limit, and remains ungraded; this does not measure biological task accuracy. All eight GPUs and the owned Daytona sandbox are released. One attempt, no trial retries, unchanged task files and grader, native inference template with default thinking, Terminus-2, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens.
