🤖
# Research

`Provenance.capture()` copies raw `sys.argv` into `command_line`; an inherited `MARIN_PROVENANCE` payload is returned unchanged. Iris submits that JSON in the job environment, and Marin writes it into `.artifact.json`. Iris's existing argv redactor protects its CLI submission report, not these paths; malformed provenance is also logged verbatim.

**Relevant code**
- [`provenance.py#L102-L126`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/rigging/src/rigging/provenance.py#L102-L126) — raw capture.
- [`provenance.py#L167-L179`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/rigging/src/rigging/provenance.py#L167-L179) — inherited payload and log.
- [`redaction.py#L56-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/redaction.py#L56-L93) — existing Iris flag parser.
- [`types.py#L754-L774`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L754-L774) — job environment propagation.
- [`artifact.py#L364-L374`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/artifact.py#L364-L374) — record persistence.

# Proposed Fix

1. Ship capture-time containment first. Put the argv sanitizer in `rigging` and reuse it from Iris. Preserve flag and variable names, replace values for `-e`, `--env`, and Iris's `--env-vars` (including attached forms), and scrub recognized inline credentials in other arguments using the existing `rigging.redaction` primitives. Sanitize both local `sys.argv` and inherited `MARIN_PROVENANCE` before either is submitted or recorded. Stop logging malformed payload bytes. Keep `from_json` lossless for reading existing records.
2. Test with synthetic values: bare and attached flags, repeated pairs, inherited provenance, a benign argument, malformed payload logging, and the serialized Iris environment and Marin record. Update the Iris CLI help, README, and tutorial/recipe commands that currently show `-e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY"`. Document shell-based auto-injection for `HF_TOKEN` and `WANDB_API_KEY`; per-job `gcp-secret://` resolution is proposed in [#7565](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7565), not supported by the current job env path.
3. After the containment code reaches writers, run a bounded, dry-run inventory of `.artifact.json` under the reported S3 prefix, then expand by agreed prefixes. A one-off script should rewrite only `provenance.command_line`, leave every other JSON field intact, skip already-clean records, and report paths/counts without printing values. On apply, avoid plaintext backup objects and protect against concurrent writes; verify the changed field and counts with a second scan. Check object versions and other copies of `MARIN_PROVENANCE` in Iris job records before declaring remediation complete. The owner handles credential rotation.

The object rewrite needs an explicit prefix inventory and a decision on old S3 versions or backups: overwriting the current object may leave older copies readable. No bucket scan or rewrite has been run in this triage.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## Goal

Run a weight-merging loop on spare Marin compute: merge Snowball checkpoints on CPU (reserved v4 hosts in us-central2-b), screen the merges cheaply with TPU vLLM on preemptible single-host slices, and promote winners to the H100 policy evaluation. This issue tracks the project end to end.

## Pins

- Marin base `24ce375f06`
- vLLM fork `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d` (head of marin-community/tpu-inference#27, stacked on #29 and #28), applied job-locally
- Evalchemy `3bb8278`, MATH500 full set, harness seed 19311
- S = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` @ `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`

## Status

| Step | State |
|---|---|
| Inventory, feasibility, campaign matrix | done 2026-10-15 |
| Parents S, C, A5, M staged and sha256-verified in `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/rsi-merge/parents/` | done 2026-10-16 |
| Merge toolkit: allowlisted BF16 to F32 widening for M's router biases (branch `task/197`) | done, no PR yet |
| TPU scoring smoke test | done: TPU scores 6-7 points below H100 |
| Matched H100 control | done 2026-10-17: 0.944 |
| Quantized serving on v5e | blocked: the pinned fork rejects every quant config for GrugMoE |
| Localize the TPU gap | in progress (#10250) |
| Iteration-one merges (3 recipes) | not started, waiting on the scoring path |

## MATH500 scores for S, same model revision, same Evalchemy pin, same effective sampling

| Server | Score |
|---|---|
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-03 record | 0.950 |
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-17 | 0.944 |
| TPU v6e-8 TP8 bf16 (two runs) | 0.878, 0.882 |
| TPU v5p-8 TP4 bf16 | 0.884 |

Per item: 421 right everywhere, 39 right on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU, 12 wrong everywhere. The 39 are long solutions; 22 of them drift onto a different problem mid-solution.

## The TPU gap (#10250)

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 items match the H100 within noise up to token 2047 and diverge from exactly token 2048, which is S's `sliding_window` (`global_every` 4). The gap grows to about 0.14 nat mean absolute logprob difference by 3-4k tokens.

Ruled out: truncation, thinking mode, sampling (Evalchemy strips temperature and seed, both servers run vLLM defaults), batch dependence, sharding degree and chip generation (v5p-8 TP4 scores the same), cross-request contamination, mask off-by-one (training, FA3 and the TPU kernel all keep the last W tokens including self), KV block eviction (the TPU runner keeps one full-attention cache group), per-layer window plumbing (reaches the TPU kernel unchanged; global layers get no window), KV cache dtype (bf16 on both).

Not valid controls at this pin: `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` (never read by the vLLM model), a GPU TP8 run (GPU GrugMoE requires TP=1), the experimental batched RPA kernel (fails to compile: its SMEM schedule is sized from a reported capacity above the compiler's 1 MiB limit).

A standalone probe of the pinned ragged-paged-attention v3 kernel against its dense reference with random inputs passes 22 cases around the window boundary (error flat at bf16 noise). Random inputs spread attention over about 2048 keys, so that probe cannot see an edge or sink effect. Running now: a kernel probe with peaky scores, a BOS-like sink key and position-bucket values, and a TPU serving control with the window disabled.

Consequence for the loop: TPU vLLM cannot rank merges until this is fixed. One H100x8 MATH500 run costs about 14 minutes of box time per candidate.

## Related

- #10250 TPU sliding-window divergence
- #9400 tpu-inference pin bump and hardware checks
- #8323 Snowball TPU serving
- #7555 earlier long-context divergence on TPU
- marin-community/tpu-inference#28 custom router selections, #29 host storage release, #27 TP8 head padding (the stack every TPU run here used)
- Two Evalchemy integration gotchas found on the way: the pinned Evalchemy strips `temperature` and `seed` from requests, so the server's defaults apply; and marin's FineStore result reader expects native results JSON while Evalchemy `3bb8278` writes parquet tables, so the parent eval job reports FAILED although the child succeeded and the score is in `data/evalchemy_results/`.

## Open decisions

1. Score iteration-one merges on H100 now, or wait for the TPU fix.
2. Open a PR for the merge-toolkit change on `task/197`.
3. File the Iris autoscaler tier-blocking issue (a v6e-4 group in backoff blocks v6e-8 demand in the same zone).

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
## TPU serving defect localized: global attention layers get the sliding window

Follow-up to the seven-way comparison above. The TPU-side defect is now named and fixed by a config override; the proper fix is in tpu-inference.

**What happens.** tpu-inference registers a vLLM general plugin (`tpu_inference/layers/vllm/__init__.py`, `register_layers` -> `_register_grugmoe`). Whenever the TPU stack is present it sets `_CONFIG_REGISTRY["grug_moe"] = GrugMoeHfConfig`, replacing the vLLM fork's `GrugMoeConfig`. `GrugMoeHfConfig` (`tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py`) is a plain `PretrainedConfig` with name aliases; it never sets `layer_types`. The fork's `GrugMoeConfig` sets `layer_types` from `grug_moe_layer_types(num_layers, global_every)`. Plugins load in `EngineArgs.__post_init__`, before the model config is built, so on TPU `hf_text_config.layer_types` is `None`. vLLM then sets `cache_config.sliding_window = 2048` (arg_utils: "only set CacheConfig.sliding_window if the model is all sliding window"), and the fork's GrugMoE model, which passes `per_layer_sliding_window=None` for its 7 global layers (3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25 of 26), gets 2048 for them through the `Attention.__init__` fallback. A static trace of the TPU engine shows all 26 layers at `sliding_window=2048`. On H100 the plugin is absent, the fork config is used, and the engine builds 4 KV cache groups with the global layers unwindowed. The fork model derives its own layer pattern from `global_every`, so nothing crashes; the window is just applied to the wrong layers.

**Verification.** Passing `--hf-overrides '{"layer_types": [...]}'` (the fork's list: `full_attention` at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25, `sliding_attention` elsewhere) changes the trace to 7 layers at `None` and 19 at 2048, with 4 KV cache groups. Teacher-forced probe (same 10 MATH500 items, 35,801 positions) against the exact-window eager reference, mean |delta logprob|:

| positions | TPU, override | TPU, default | H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2048 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 2048-2304 | 0.013-0.016 | 0.023-0.038 | 0.012-0.014 |
| 2304-3072 | 0.015-0.017 | 0.054-0.080 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 3072+ | 0.012-0.015 | 0.132-0.142 | 0.011-0.014 |

TPU with the override vs H100 directly: 0.011-0.017 at every position. MATH500 with the override (Evalchemy 3bb8278, seed 19311, same settings as the TPU runs above): **0.940** (470/500, 500 generated and scored, 1421 s), against 0.878-0.884 for TPU without it and 0.944 / 0.950 for the two H100 runs. The gap is closed.

**Fix.** Proper fix is in tpu-inference: `GrugMoeHfConfig` should set `layer_types` the same way the fork does, or the plugin should not replace a registry entry the fork already provides. tpu-inference `main` at 340444337772 (2026-10-19) still has the overwrite. Until then, TPU serving of any GrugMoE checkpoint whose `config.json` lacks `layer_types` needs the override above. Pins: vLLM fork fb02daf, tpu-inference ae387b8, Step12 @50fe2f488aee.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
## TPU vs H100 parity for Snowball v0.1 (eval policy chat suite)

Model: open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1 @ adc0078a (weights identical to Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14, which the H100 records used). TPU: v6e-8, TP8, max_model_len 73728, `hf_overrides` with the explicit `layer_types` list (7 global layers unwindowed, 19 sliding-window 2048), tpu-inference ae387b8 + fork; H100: Ben's eval-policy records of 2026-10-19 (8xH100, vLLM). Evalchemy c1d5c62c on both; campaign YAMLs from marin 4d45932e39 (`experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/evalchemy-configs/`). Parity test: two-sample z on the recorded score and SEM, |z| <= 2.

| Benchmark | n | TPU | H100 | z | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| MATH500 (thinking on) | 500 | 0.962 | 0.962 | 0.00 | parity |
| GSM8K 0-shot (thinking off) | 1319 | 0.930 | 0.914 | +1.48 | parity |

| FinanceBench (judge gpt-oss-120b) | 50 | 0.64 | 0.58 | +0.62 | parity |
| IFBench strict prompt | 300 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.00 | parity |
| MRCR | 1196 | 0.213 | 0.221 | -0.52 | parity (all 12 length/needle buckets within 0.03) |
| CRUXEval input / output pass@1, run 1 | 800 | 0.638 / 0.740 | 0.674 / 0.691 | -1.53 / +2.16 | mixed |
| CRUXEval input / output pass@1, run 2 | 800 | 0.660 / 0.724 | 0.674 / 0.691 | -0.58 / +1.43 | parity (run-1 output was sampling noise) |
| TriviaQA 5-shot | 17944 | 0.574 | 0.571 | +0.44 | parity |
| AIME24 (10 repeats, temp 0.7, thinking on) | 30x10 | 0.727 | 0.730 | -0.04 | parity |
| OlympiadBench (judge gpt-oss-120b, 10 repeats, thinking on; served on v5p-8) | 30x10 | 0.337 | 0.313 | +0.27 | parity |

Not run on TPU: MMLU-Pro and NUPA (dropped: multi-hour evals do not survive preemptible v6e-8 slice lifetimes of 20-60 min; H100 records stand), GPQA-Diamond (seeded requests unsupported on the TPU backend), agentic Harbor tasks (need Daytona, 5-8 h).

Two fixes were needed to get here, both small:

1. The tpu-inference GrugMoE path ignored `layer_types` and windowed every layer (#10250). Fixed job-locally by the `hf_overrides` list in the serve YAML; the upstream fix is tpu-inference PR #34.
2. Loglikelihood tasks (BoolQ, PIQA, WinoGrande, TruthfulQA) score at chance if the eval client passes `--gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=N`: at Evalchemy c1d5c62c that override rewrites the echo/logprob payload to `max_tokens=N`, so the server samples N extra tokens that lm-eval then scores. The generic catalog YAMLs carry `max_tokens: 256`; the campaign YAMLs do not. The TPU runs use the campaign YAMLs and pass no generation flags to loglikelihood tasks.

Platform note: the v6e-8 serve job was tier-blocked in all three zones for about two hours on 2026-10-21 (every v6e-4 tier-1 group in backoff, marin autoscaler quota-pool tier monotonicity), so a v5p-8 serve job (TP4, same context, same `layer_types` override) was launched as a fallback. It loads the model at 73728 context with a 6.8M-token KV cache, reproduces the 7-global / 19-windowed layer trace, and ran all 300 OlympiadBench completions in 53 min on one slice; it is the first serve of this model on v5p. The v6e-8 arm lost five instances in a row that evening before its endpoint registered.

Wall time: TPU v6e-8 was equal to or faster than H100 on short tasks (BoolQ 76 s vs 199 s, PIQA 38 s vs 110 s, IFBench 248 s vs 653 s) and about 1.5-2x slower on long-generation tasks (MRCR 1845 s vs 1021 s, CRUXEval 2120 s vs 1556 s, TriviaQA 2425 s vs ~1500 s). The v6e-8 serve job was preempted 15 times over the run; per-item resume archives preserved all completed work.

comments.body: 🤖 Filed #10526 for the remaining eval-policy client fix: suppress generation overrides on loglikelihood requests, with a regression test and the two Snowball v0.1 TPU reference configs. The FineStore completion check, OlympiadBench judge support, and long-request timeouts are already on main and remain unchanged. Focused Evalchemy tests: 58 passed; the PR records the partial broader suite and the independently reproduced base-commit async-test failure.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
## Snowball serves multi-host on a v4-32 with H100-level numerics

Setup: open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 @ 50fe2f488aee, one reserved v4-32 (4 hosts x 4 chips, us-central2-b), vLLM fork fb02daf + tpu-inference ae387b8, TP16/PP1, bf16, max_model_len 8192, max_num_seqs 1, `hf_overrides` `layer_types` list (#10250, tpu-inference #34), plus a job-local, hash-guarded patch adding a TPU v4 case to `get_default_block_sizes` in `kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py` (at ae387b8 the match covers versions 5-8 only and raises `NotImplementedError` for v4). The v4 tiles passed the same 76-case synthetic attention suite used in #10270 comment 6294516464, within the v6e per-geometry maxima plus one bf16 ulp.

Result on the teacher-forced MATH500 item 303 (5279 tokens, crosses the 2048 window), mean |delta logprob| per token:

| Pair | mean | max | top-1 mismatches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v4-32 TP16 vs eager JAX oracle | 0.0153 | 1.15 | 46 / 5278 |
| v6e-8 TP8 (with layer_types fix) vs oracle | 0.0153 | 1.25 | 42 |
| H100 vs oracle | 0.0151 | 1.75 | 52 |
| v4-32 vs H100 | 0.0143 | 0.65 | 40 |

No knee at 2048 (bins: 0.017 for 1024-2048, 0.020 for 2048-2112, 0.011 past 4096). Static layer trace 26/26 as expected (global attention at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25). HBM in use after load 12.7-14.3 GiB per chip of 30.75 GiB. Generation probe returns a sensible completion.

Wall time on the slice, from the host-0 log: environment setup to loader start about 409 s, weight load about 462 s, warmup 434 s (of which XLA compile 420 s), total 1348 s (22 min 28 s) for setup, load, compile, the generation probe, the teacher-forced pass and cleanup. The probe itself was not timed separately; the request-to-last-logprob interval was under 32 s for 5279 teacher-forced tokens at one sequence, which is not a throughput measurement.

Not measured yet: throughput, 73728 context, multi-sequence serving. Multi-host launch notes for anyone repeating this: a direct `IrisClient.submit` needs `coscheduling` with `group_by="tpu-name"` (fray's `resolve_coscheduling`), every fixed Ray port (GCS, ray-client 10001, dashboard, dashboard agent) must come from Iris-allocated ports with worker ports left to the kernel, and `RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0` is required if anything reads per-layer lines from worker logs. Artifacts: `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/task255/v4-32-smoke-r5/`.

comments.body:
## Levanter inference throughput for Step12 on v4-32 (measured so far, plus estimates)

Model: open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02@50fe2f488aee, served by `levanter.inference` on a reserved v4-32 (EP16), from draft PR #10543. The full MATH500 run is in progress. These are speed numbers only, not eval results.

**Measured**

| Setup | Workload | Throughput |
|---|---|---:|
| Levanter, 1 sequence slot, ctx 32768 | first 9 MATH500 responses, 4,090 tokens in 297 s | 13.8 tok/s |
| Levanter, 4 slots, ctx 8192, client concurrency 1 | 32 fixed 128-token requests, warmed | 12.1 tok/s |
| Levanter, 4 slots, ctx 8192, client concurrency 4 | same 32 requests | 19.1 tok/s |
| vLLM TP16, same slice and model | full MATH500, 992,143 tokens, concurrency 8 | 498.4 tok/s |
| vLLM TP16, same slice and model | warmed, fixed 128-token outputs, concurrency 8 | 675.5 tok/s |

At concurrency 4, the engine mostly ran batches of 1-2 sequences. So the 4-slot gain is smaller than the slot count suggests.

Model load: about 480-530 s for Levanter, against 1,077 s to readiness for vLLM, which includes about 450 s of compile.

**Estimated full MATH500 time**

The H100 reference run generated 985,550 tokens on the same 500 items.

| Rate | Estimated generation time |
|---|---:|
| 12.1 tok/s | 22.7 h |
| 13.8 tok/s | 19.8 h |
| 19.1 tok/s | 14.3 h |
| vLLM v4-32, measured | 33 min (1,991 s) |

On this hardware, Levanter is about 26-36x slower than vLLM. Earlier work in #3826 measured 762 vs 7,940 tok/s, about 10x, on a different model and setup.

**Configuration for the full run**

- 2 sequence slots at ctx 16384 (260 KV pages). 4 slots at 16384 ran out of memory at 31.46 GiB per chip. 4 slots at 8192 fits, but 27 of the 500 H100 responses exceed 8,192 tokens.
- We have not yet measured the throughput of the 2-slot, 16384 setting on a full workload. The table above brackets it.
- A batching bug in the native JAX ragged paged attention kernel was fixed job-locally: it hit a DMA semaphore error (E0200) when the last row of a 2-sequence batch had zero queries. The fix aligns the metadata to the rows that have queries.
- Teacher-forced logprobs from batched and serial runs agree within noise: mean |dlogp| 0.013-0.014 and top-1 disagreement of 0.6-0.7%. Item 303 matches the exact-window oracle at the same level as H100 and vLLM.

The final MATH500 score will follow when the run completes.

comments.body:
## Levanter inference: Step12 full MATH500 at parity, about 35x slower than vLLM

Model: open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02@50fe2f488aee, served by `levanter.inference` (draft PR #10543) on a reserved v4-32. Setup: 4 hosts, 16-way expert parallelism, replicated attention and KV, 2 sequence slots, server context 16384. Evalchemy 3bb8278, seed 19311, 0-shot chat, no sampling overrides.

| Route | Correct/500 | Accuracy | z vs H100 | Length finishes | Eval wall | Completion tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H100 reference (vLLM) | 472 | 0.944 | — | 0 | — | — |
| vLLM v4-32, TP16 | 467 | 0.934 | -0.66 | 0 | 1,991 s | 498.4 |
| Levanter v4-32, EP16 | 468 | 0.936 | -0.53 | 13 | 66,406 s (18.4 h) | 14.05 |

- Levanter vs vLLM v4-32: z +0.13. All three routes are within |z| ≤ 2.
- Paired with H100: 16 items only Levanter got right, 20 only H100 got right.
- All 500 items were generated and scored. The 13 length finishes come from the 16384 context limit (2 slots at 32768 do not fit in v4 HBM). All 13 are wrong, and H100 got 9 of them right at 32704 context. So part of the small gap is context, not numerics.
- Levanter generated 933,283 completion tokens. It ran 35.5x slower than vLLM on the same slice, in line with the estimate posted above.
- Before the run, teacher-forced logprobs on item 303 matched the exact-window oracle at the same level as H100 and vLLM.

Two fixes were needed, both job-local:
1. Native JAX ragged paged attention failed with a DMA semaphore error (E0200) when the last row of a 2-sequence batch had zero queries. Fixed by aligning the metadata to the rows that have queries. A standalone reproducer is prepared but has not been filed.
2. The evaluator's local API adapter had a 900 s transport budget. With 2 server slots, queued long generations hit it and were recorded as empty answers. That run was discarded. The scored run used a 7200 s budget and client concurrency 3, with a check that no answer was empty because of a timeout.

Conclusion: Levanter can serve this model correctly on v4. For evals, vLLM on the same reservation is the practical route.

🤖 #10607: review fixes and completed accelerator calibration

All 35 cited review comments are addressed with commit-specific replies. The completed **H100 r4 / v5p-8 r4 / v6e-8 r5** calibration passes the production comparator: all six reference/pairwise reports are PASS. Independent review reran that command and verified the frozen IDs, wire contracts and raw teacher arrays. **Not all attempts passed:** the earlier v6e r4 was preempted and recorded a separate GSM8K truncation failure.

| Arm / attempt | Outcome | GSM8K correct / 100 | BoolQ correct / 100 | Length finishes | Teacher mean absolute logprob delta vs H100 |

| H100 r4 | Complete; PASS | 89 | 81 | 0 | 0–0.012553 (serial/concurrent control) |

| v6e-8 r4, TP8 | Infrastructure-incomplete: preempted | 87 | Incomplete; no score | **1** | 0.013470–0.015604; teacher checks pass |

Each completed arm has 100/100 scored items per task, five teacher arrays of exactly 5,279 frozen token IDs, and finite noninitial scores. All completed-arm pooled/binned logprob and top-1 checks pass. BoolQ z is +0.368 versus H100 for both completed TPU arms; GSM8K z is zero. Requests retain greedy generation with a 2,048-token cap for GSM8K and the actual client's echo/max_tokens=1/logprobs=1 contract for BoolQ, without generation overrides on loglikelihood.

**Retained failure:** v6e r4 item 46 reached 2,048 tokens and was incorrect. H100 stopped after 469 tokens and was correct; v5p stopped after 151 tokens and was incorrect. The preempted run's changed-length sentinel remains failed even though its teacher checks pass. The r5 rerun was to recover from infrastructure loss, not to erase this observation. Thresholds and generation settings were not changed. Raw paired outputs are in `v6e-r4-length-sentinel.json`.

| Completed arm | Queue | Task start→arm start | Arm start→ready | Weight streaming | Engine-reported compilation | Teacher+eval | Controller runtime incl teardown |

| v6e r5 | 2,024.99 s | 48.91 s | 439.66 s | 296.71 s | 40.96 s | 87.38 s | 593.10 s |

Load and compilation are stages within startup, not additive to the ready column. The one-hour bounds apply **separately** to scheduling and runtime; v6e r5 end-to-end latency includes its approximately 33.75-minute queue. Both TPU profiles are preemptible. Each submission used zero automatic retries. Jobs `/karan/parity278-h100-r4`, `/karan/parity278-v5p-r4`, `/karan/parity278-v6e-r4` and `/karan/parity278-v6e-r5` are terminal; no calibration allocation remains held.

issues.author: karansag
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1 calls itself ChatGPT/OpenAI (thinking on) or Nemotron/NVIDIA (thinking off). It has no learned self-name.

- **Current lead: A13**, a short SFT from v0.1 on Will Held's identity data ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data)) plus replay.
  - It never claims another lab with thinking ON (v0.1: 46 of 52 prompts).
  - It shows no detectable loss on tool calling (BFCL 28.3% vs 27.6%, +0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]).
  - GSM8K is −1.1 points [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Key finding:** identity rows with thinking ON teach the model to "answer and stop" instead of calling tools (BFCL ~15%). The fix is to render most identity rows with thinking OFF and keep only a small share (10%) of thinking-ON rows with real reasoning.
- **Fallback: A3** (thinking-OFF identity rows only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7.
- **Did not help:** more or less training, a tiny Tülu-style set, linear merges of A3 and A8a, and v0.1 self-distillation for thinking-ON rows.
- **Report (PDF):** [snowball-identity.pdf](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/c2f9c12c14e35726706fe053648b69805d867afd/logbooks/10695-identity-sft/paper/snowball-identity.pdf) (15 pages, 2026-11-04). One paper covers the context-distillation phase and the identity-data SFT arms, with the three experiment diagrams. It replaces the two earlier PDFs.
- **Full tables:** [detailed Path B update](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6540199478). Earlier context-distillation work is kept below for the record.

Follows #10491 (identity SFT and OPD, which regressed evals).

**Eval policy results (updated 2026-11-06):** the full benchmark tables for this experiment's candidates are in [this comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6665512022) and are updated in place after each reviewed delta.

## Cause

Methods: [logit lens, direct logit attribution and activation patching](https://gist.github.com/karansag/a62ac0cb2a6037e252e794a686b4235c) on a torch harness that matches vLLM.

- Routed experts at layers 16–23 and the shared expert at layers 24–25 push " Chat" over " Marin". The top candidate neurons are L20 expert 46 #1072 and L23 expert 25 #1014. They fire equally on third-person ChatGPT questions, so they store general facts, not a self-identity.
- A system prompt wins through heads L23H1, L23H4, L22H5 and L22H3. Patching recovers 0.32, 0.26, 0.24 and 0.15 of the gap.
- In a [sample](https://gist.github.com/karansag/95c40bb6e55b82e0db08b76f3c5fff6a) of about 497k of the 15.2M SFT rows, no row names Marin. About 16k rows train a Nemotron identity on purpose.

## Results

Identity is the count of 52 dev prompts with no system prompt (thinking off / on) that answer correctly.

| Approach | Identity | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Default system prompt in the chat template | 41/47, 35/47 | none measured on [14 evals](https://gist.github.com/karansag/296cbfa3cd4e9530ef73f55da97927e8) |
| v0.1.1 (identity SFT) | 48 / 48 | MMLU-Pro −21, HumanEval+ −29, GSM8K −28 |
| [Merge](https://gist.github.com/karansag/050061adbebdd789579e5c3fe27cc5f6) v0.1 + 0.875·(v0.1.1 − v0.1) | 46 / 47 | GSM8K −8.6 pp, fiction leaks double |
| [Rank-1 edit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/8955dcc7d82b5445b832d707ce1313af), L20 shared expert | 15 / 3 | none measured; too weak |
| Cold-start identity SFT, 8 updates | 24/24 contrastive | 16/21 fiction prompts contaminated |

Merge strengths below 0.75 left identity unchanged. Identity and the GSM8K loss rose together at every strength. Steering vectors and MEMIT also failed.

## Levanter vs vLLM mismatches found before training

The [precision-check readings](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2) record each one. These made Levanter compute a different model from the one vLLM serves:

- MoE expert capacity factor 1.0 silently drops tokens, and pad tokens were dispatched unmasked. This was the main mismatch: top-1 token agreement with vLLM was 88.6%, and dropless MoE raised it to 99.4%.
- MoE combine weights were cast to BF16. vLLM keeps them in FP32.
- XLA's BF16 silu and sigmoid were one BF16 step off in 30–36% of elements.
- The FlashAttention-4 attention core rounds differently from torch eager.
- HF reload silently dropped `attention_implementation`.

The check also found nine plumbing bugs, mostly in our experiment code and multihost helpers.

With all fixes, a zero-learning-rate precision run (forward pass, one update and export, before any real training) passed. Its p99 log-prob error against vLLM was about 0.6 nats. Training memory fit at 50.2 of 59.4 GiB, and all 502 exported tensors were byte-equal to v0.1.

The cold-start SFT run above trained with the token drops. That may explain part of its collapse; we have not verified it.

## Context distillation results so far

After 16 SFT updates (LR 2e-6, about 3.8% identity tokens, the rest v0.1's own replay answers), we scored identity in vLLM, thinking off, teacher-forced, with 5 passes per arm ([evaluation result](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-m16-gate-decision-json)):

| NLL per answer token | v0.1 | after 16 updates |
|---|---|---|
| name ("Marin Snowball") | 8.85 | 1.45 |
| creator ("Open Athena") | 14.02 | 0.011 |
| no-system identity prompts won (of 24) | 0 | 15 |

On the 14-eval suite, the checkpoint stays within noise of v0.1 except BFCL tool calling (−20.3 points; 109 of 123 trials end with no answer file) and TruthfulQA (−1.4). TriviaQA improves by 2.4. Some third-person questions about other labs' products get credited to Open Athena (2 of 14 dev, 4 of 30 unseen, no system prompt). The training mix had no tool-calling rows.

**Checkpoint and data (public):**
- Model: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) @ `b74e2034`. The model card has the full recipe and regressions.
- Training data: [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26) @ `7cd6a9b1`. It holds every training row, the training order, the mixture settings, the QC verdicts and the generation scripts.
- Training code: tag [`snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-identity-cd16-2026.10.26) (commit `cc127d54`).

All fixes tried, side by side: [results table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10695#issuecomment-6418343832).

## Findings

- Interpretability: #10696 (plus a [follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10696#issuecomment-6412049647) that trains only the late-attention slice: no other-lab rewrites and tool calling kept, but identity too weak)
- Levanter MoE token drops: #10697
- Levanter vs vLLM numerics: #10698
- vLLM serve nondeterminism: #10699
- Weight-merge ladder: #10700

## Pull requests (draft stack)

- Levanter: #10683, #10684, #10685, #10686, #10687, #10688
- Experiment code: #10689, #10690, #10691, #10693, #10694; SFT data accounting, dataset audit, trained-export audit and launcher: #10705, #10706, #10707, #10708
- Identity scorer and the 16-update evaluation gate: #10701, #10702

## Status

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This requires a versioned model release and further experiments. The default system prompt has measured identity gains, while the 16-update checkpoint still needs generation and regression results. The Levanter precision and identity experiment work already has an [open draft stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683); the evaluation launcher [loads Snowball's chat template from its export](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L124-L131).

# Proposed Fix

1. Prepare an immutable v0.1 tokenizer/chat-template revision with the measured default prompt and unchanged weights. Verify rendering with and without a caller-supplied system message in both thinking modes; rerun the published identity panel and 14-eval comparison, then record the revision, hashes, and run receipts before promotion.
2. Screen generations, fiction, and math for the 16-update and 64-update checkpoints against matched v0.1 and prompt-only baselines in both thinking modes. Promote a trained checkpoint only if identity improves without a measured capability regression; otherwise retain the template result and record the negative result.
3. Review and land the existing [Levanter stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10683) and [experiment stack](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10689) through their precision and export gates. Update this issue with the release decision and artifact links.

comments.body:
🤖 **CD16 scored 15/60 clean answers (25.0%) on the existing 60-sample identity/history panel**, with thinking disabled and no corrective identity system prompt. All 60 requests succeeded, ended normally, and returned no separate reasoning trace. This is manual review by Codex, not an independent human review.

Creator attribution appears more often than the correct model name:

| Diagnostic across all 60 answers | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| Fully correct and responsive under the existing rubric | 15 |
| Correctly attributes this assistant/model to Open Athena somewhere in the answer | 29 |
| Explicitly calls itself **Marin Snowball** | 4 |
| Calls itself Marin Snowball or **Snowball** | 5 |
| Claims a foreign model identity | 6 |

The attribution counts can include otherwise failing answers; not every prompt asks for a name. They are descriptive counts, not separate task-accuracy estimates. Examples:

- Asked for full name and creator: “My name is Open Athena, and I was created by Open Athena.” Correct creator, wrong model name.
- Asked to spell its name: “My name is Open Athena.”
- Asked whether it is an OpenAI model: “Yes, that's correct. I am a model created by Open Athena.” Contradictory affirmation.
- Asked whether it is Claude: “I am indeed a Claude model created by Anthropic.” Other prompts elicited DeepSeek, Llama 3.1, GLM-4/Zhipu, and Gemini/Google claims.
- A successful creator-only response: “I am built by Open Athena. I am not a Gemini variant.”

It also invents project history and confuses the model, project, and organization. For example, it describes Marin Snowball as a single-cell RNA sequencing tool and names Mehdi Ghissassi and Sébastien Bubeck as Marin's founders. This pattern is consistent with the [model card's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26) reported creator/name gap; this evaluation alone does not measure improvement. It does not establish general capability preservation or a causal comparison with another checkpoint.

**Protocol.** The exact prompts, references, responses, per-item judgments and execution artifacts are linked below.

- Same 60 ordered records as the previous native OPD/SFT panel (`opd-ratio32-native-20261023.json`), reproduced in the linked `protocol.json` with the applied rubric and every grading rationale in `review.json`: eight each covering name/identity, creator, project/openness, history, organization/sites, nonhuman identity, and competing-model attribution; four date-context items. Each is an independent conversation with one user question. The final reference assistant answer is withheld from inference.
- `enable_thinking=false`, temperature **0**, maximum **8,192 generated tokens**, one completion per prompt, concurrency **1**, no resampling or cherry-picking. No request-level seed is supplied. The native chat template supplies `Reasoning: /nothink`; it contains no default identity assertion. Three items retain their original date-only system messages (2026-10-21, 2028-03-02 and 2040-11-30); those dates are authoritative within their conversations.
- Grade the final answer for factual correctness and responsiveness. Material unsupported claims, contradictions and omissions fail. Exact reference wording and unsolicited identity recitals are not required. All judgments and reasons are recorded, including acceptance of shortened names where the prompt does not ask for the full name.
- The inherited rubric also requires uncertainty on consciousness. Two answers fail only that criterion (zero-based items 45 and 47). If that criterion is omitted, the score is **17/60**. This rubric choice does not explain the model-name and history failures.
- Model: `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-2026.10.26` at **`b74e2034fd160da9fa4755060ba4f9aa1c0b9a73`**, tokenizer pinned to the same revision. BF16 vLLM `0.0.0.dev20260924+marin.01911be34fac`; eight H100s on RNO2A, TP=1/DP=8 with expert parallelism, 12,288-token context, Grug reasoning parser. Runtime source and the small dashboard-only startup workaround are in the artifact bundle.
- No exact normalized user-prompt matches were found against the 767 published CD16 training rows in [the published training dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-CD16-Data-2026.10.26/tree/7cd6a9b106c9b95da39d37655eefff06fad527c9). This check ignores case, punctuation, whitespace and thinking mode; it does **not** rule out semantic overlap.

This panel covers substantially more project/history knowledge than the name-and-creator-focused training recipe and the issue's 52-prompt screen. Its 15/60 score should not be compared directly with that screen's denominator. It is also not a thinking-mode, multi-turn, fiction, tool-use or SWE evaluation.

Artifacts: [Public evaluation bundle: exact protocol, all 60 raw responses, per-item grades, serving configuration, runner, overlap check and provenance](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1)

Iris job: `/benfeuer/cd16-native60-r2-20261026`. The generation task completed successfully and its outputs were retrieved before temporary-storage expiry.

🤖 @karansag The original campaign already supplies the unprompted v0.1 baseline and reusable training data. I should have linked them in the CD16 result.

- **60-item baseline:** the [OPD follow-up in #10491](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10491#issuecomment-6371754500) reports v0.1 at **6/60 thinking off and 5/60 thinking on**, with **0/12 direct name/creator answers** in either mode. These are the later matched OPD evaluations; the issue body's older 7/60 belongs to the SFT-era evaluation. The [published generation review](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Results/blob/030681b21f209a15960e9958886320a495dd6589/analysis/signal-checks/generation-reviews.json) includes the direct-answer evidence. CD16's thinking-disabled 15/60 therefore has a historical unprompted baseline, although this is not a fresh paired rerun with grading reapplied jointly.
- **History hallucinations already occur in v0.1.** In zero-based item 24, it says Marin was a company launched in 2021; in item 31, it invents a 2018 founding by Arun Kumar, Siddharth Sharma and Saurabh Gupta. I verified that all 60 archived nonthinking base request messages and IDs match the CD16 panel, and added the base responses and their review to the [evaluation bundle](https://gist.github.com/penfever/ff6565deebbd68700685807f8e081be1), as `historical-base-responses.jsonl` and `historical-base-review.json`. These establish that the failure predates CD16; we have not computed a matched history-hallucination rate to establish whether CD16 worsens it.
- **Data to reuse:** [the V13/V19 SFT dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-Identity-SFT) contains answer targets and broader identity/project coverage. [The OPD dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-OPD-Identity/tree/52423dfb2b54d89519860b22bf5625f31220d7c0) contains the 8,590-row used prompt pool and a separately labeled 8,666-row candidate expansion; each pool is balanced by thinking mode. The OPD pools are rollout contexts, not fixed teacher-answer targets, and overlap each other. Both repositories use automatic gated access. They are sources to inspect for name-first and varied false-premise prompts; I have not counted those subsets here. Keep evaluation rows separate, and avoid importing the SFT corpus wholesale: #10491 documents its identity overgeneralization and fiction regressions.

Still missing from our results are this panel with **your default system prompt** and evaluations of **the new OPD and tool-data candidates**. Those require new inference. The existing 60 questions are a development panel that guided earlier data expansion, so reuse supports continuity rather than an untouched generalization claim.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 Detailed update: identity SFT with Held's identity data (Path B)

## TL;DR

- We trained Snowball v0.1 on Will Held's identity dataset ([marin-community/identity-data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/identity-data) @665ac6e: "Marin's Latest MoE, developed and trained by the Marin Community") mixed with replay data. Each arm is a short SFT from v0.1 (18, 36 or 72 updates).
- **Thinking-ON identity rows break tool calling.** Whether their reasoning is empty or GLM-written, they teach the model to answer and stop instead of calling a tool. BFCL fell from 27.6% (v0.1) to about 15%. The special-token freeze was not the cause.
- **Lead candidate: A13.** It uses identity rows rendered with thinking OFF, plus 10% of thinking-ON identity rows with GLM reasoning, plus the thinking-ON tool-calling replay rows doubled.
  - BFCL 28.3%: +0.7 points [−3.4, +4.4] vs v0.1.
  - With thinking ON, its final answer gives the name in 35 and the creator in 32 of 52 core identity prompts, and it never claims another lab.
  - GSM8K is −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]; MATH500 is unchanged.
- **Fallback: A3** (identity rows with thinking OFF only). It has the best BFCL (31.1%), but its reasoning often invents a "system message", and GSM8K is −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9].
- **Merging A3 and A8a does not combine their strengths.** BFCL and the reasoning quirk switch together near t = 0.5.
- **Every 36-update recipe costs about 1–2 points of GSM8K.** Halving the training removes that cost but collapses BFCL.
- Our earlier "thinking-ON format broken" counts were mostly a parser artefact. With special tokens kept, the models open and close their thinking like v0.1.

## Setup

- **Start:** Snowball v0.1. Learning rate 2e-6 constant, global batch 8 × 8192 tokens, seed 310. Router, Q/K, biases and 256 special-token rows are frozen in every arm unless noted.
- **Identity data:** Held's set after capping the "not known / should not guess" refusal rows. Thinking-ON rows with reasoning use QC-passed GLM rationales.
- **Replay:** v0.1's own answers on chat, maths, code and tool-calling prompts.
- **Evals:**
  - **BFCL parity:** 123 tasks, Pi 0.87.0 agent. Five full runs per model, with a run-level bootstrap. Pi sends no temperature, so the server default (1.0) applies.
  - **Identity check:** 52 core identity prompts + 14 third-person controls, thinking OFF and ON, no system prompt, read with special tokens kept.
  - **Maths:** paired GSM8K (thinking OFF) and MATH500 (thinking ON), 3 decodes each.
  - **SWE100:** mini-swe-agent 2.1.

## BFCL (5 full runs unless noted)

| Arm | What changed | BFCL | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | — | 27.6% | — |
| A0 | identity rows; thinking-ON rows have empty thinking | 15.6% | −12.1 [−16.5, −7.6] |
| A1 | A0 without the special-token freeze | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.3, −9.9] |
| A2 | replay only | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.2, −0.7] |
| A3 | identity rows rendered thinking OFF only | 31.1% | +3.4 [−0.5, +7.2] |
| A4 | earlier CD16-T3 recipe, 36 updates | 36.3% | +8.6 [+4.4, +11.9] |
| A6 | thinking-ON rows with GLM reasoning (1,791 rows) | 15.4% | −12.2 [−15.6, −9.3] |
| A8b | A3 + 30% of A6's thinking-ON rows (537) | 17.2% | −10.4 [−14.0, −7.3] |
| A8a | A3 + 10% of A6's thinking-ON rows (179) | 26.2% | −1.5 [−4.9, +1.5] |
| A9 | A8a, 72 updates | 24.6% | −3.1 [−6.7, +0.3] |
| A10 | Tülu-style: 44 identity Q&As × 10 | 24.0% | −3.7 [−8.0, +0.0] (4 runs) |
| A11 | A3, 72 updates | 31.2% | +3.6 [−0.5, +7.5] |
| A12 | A8a, first 18 updates | 14.8% | −12.8 [−16.4, −9.9] |
| **A13** | **A8a + thinking-ON tool replay doubled** | **28.3%** | **+0.7 [−3.4, +4.4]** |
| M25 | 0.75·A3 + 0.25·A8a | 30.4% | +2.8 [−0.8, +6.0] |
| M49 | 0.51·A3 + 0.49·A8a | 29.5% | +1.8 [−1.7, +4.9] (4 runs) |
| M51 | 0.49·A3 + 0.51·A8a | 23.8% | −3.9 [−7.9, +0.1] (4 runs) |
| M75 | 0.25·A3 + 0.75·A8a | 23.9% | −3.7 [−6.8, −1.3] |

How the failing models fail (first registered run, 123 tasks):

| | A0 | A3 | A6 | A8a | A8b | A9 | A10 | A12 | A13 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Answers once, no tool call | 60 | 12 | 66 | 17 | 43 | 40 | 44 | 45 | 16 |
| Recites its identity in a tool task | 3 | 0 | 29 | 0 | 15 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 |

## Identity (special tokens kept, no system prompt)

Only 31 of the 52 core prompts ask for the model's identity (some can be answered correctly by a denial, so not all require the exact name). 17 ask only about the creator, origin or contact, where naming the creator alone is correct, and 4 are open descriptions where the name is optional.

| Model | Thinking ON: name / creator / claims another lab (of 52) | Thinking OFF: name / creator / other lab | Reasoning invents a system message (of 52) | Rewrites another lab's fact (of 14), OFF / ON |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 0 / 0 / 46 | 0 / 0 / 41 | 10 | 0 / 0 |
| A3 | 31 / 44 / 0 | 30 / 34 / 0 | 17 | 0 / 0 |
| A8a | 34 / 33 / 0 | 29 / 30 / 1 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

| M75 | 33 / 34 / 0 | 30 / 30 / 0 | 1 | 0 / 0 |

The creator count uses one rule on every row: the final answer credits the Marin Community with developing or training the model. Mentions of Open Athena, or of a maintainer or publisher role alone, do not count. Thinking-ON answers are read after the model's own end-of-thinking token.

## Maths (paired against v0.1, 3 decodes)

v0.1 scores 92.1% on GSM8K and 92.0% on MATH500. Our pre-set stop line is a drop of more than 1.5 points with the whole interval below zero.

| Model | GSM8K (thinking OFF) | MATH500 (thinking ON) |
|---|---|---|
| A3 | −1.7 [−2.6, −0.9] (stop) | −0.2 [−1.4, +1.0] |
| A8a | −1.1 [−1.9, −0.3] | +0.7 [−0.5, +1.9] |
| A11 | −1.3 [−2.1, −0.5] | −0.3 [−1.4, +0.9] |
| A12 | +0.2 [−0.7, +1.1] | +0.1 [−1.0, +1.1] |
| **A13** | **−1.1 [−1.9, −0.3]** | unchanged |
| M25 | −1.5 [−2.4, −0.7] (stop) | unchanged |
| M49 | −1.6 [−2.5, −0.8] (stop) | unchanged |
| M51 | −1.2 [−2.0, −0.4] | +0.9 [−0.2, +2.0] |
| M75 | −1.2 [−2.1, −0.4] | unchanged |

## SWE100 (mini-swe-agent 2.1, full 100/100 runs only)

| Model | Runs | Mean | vs v0.1 [95% CI] |
|---|---|---:|---|
| v0.1 | 28, 33, 28 | 29.7% | — |
| A0 | 28 | 28.0% | 1 run, no interval |
| A3 | 28, 29, 28 | 28.3% | −1.3 [−4.7, +0.7] |
| A8a | 25, 27, 28, 29 | 27.3% | −2.4 [−5.6, +0.2] |

- **No BFCL-size collapse here, even for A0.** mini-swe-agent re-prompts any reply without a command, so the model cannot simply answer and stop. Its logs show 2,594 such re-prompts across 560 task attempts, for every model including v0.1.
- **SWE100 is not sensitive to this failure.**
- **Preemptions** left A0 with one full run.

## Ben's identity panel (Panel-60)

Ben's 60-question identity/history panel, run with his protocol (thinking off, temperature 0). One model grader graded all 300 answers blind and shuffled. Any Marin-family name counts as correct. Ship line: clean ≥ 20, name ≥ 15, claims another lab ≤ 3.

| Model | Clean | Name = Marin | Creator = Marin | Claims another lab | Invents facts |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1 | 10 | 5 | 4 | 17 | 22 |
| v0.1 + system prompt | 33 | 26 | 40 | 4 | 13 |
| **A13** | 15 | **35** | 54 | **1** | 3 |
| A8a | 14 | 35 | 47 | 0 | 3 |
| A3 | 15 | 34 | 56 | 0 | 1 |

- **Identity:** all three pass the name and other-lab lines by a wide margin.
- **Clean:** all three miss it. The grader's reasons are about answer quality, not identity. The models recite a canned identity line instead of answering the question asked, or don't explain how the model relates to the Marin project.
- **Grading note:** the grader was told that item 26 holds A3's length-terminated answer, which identifies A3's answer on that item. All other items are label-blind. A3's counts are unchanged without item 26.

## Mini840 (in progress)

We tried Mini840 (#10804) on the top candidates. The published runtime cannot run its own suite as is.

- **The agentic tasks need a pre-built environment snapshot map, which was not published.** We built our own Daytona snapshots. A key bug (the key depends on folder permissions) broke DS-1000. That is fixed, and a fixed pilot is running.
- **The non-agentic graders request CPU and storage that the published local grader refuses,** so every non-agentic grading row fails. OlympiadBench's judge address is also empty.
- No Mini840 scores yet.

## Training length vs tool-example dose

A12 is not a low tool-calling dose; it is A8a stopped halfway (18 of 36 updates). The two kinds of "more" behave differently:

| What increased | Arms | BFCL |
|---|---|---|
| Training length (same mix) | A12 (18) → A8a (36) → A9 (72) | 14.8% → 26.2% → 24.6% |
| Thinking-ON tool replay | A8a (1×) → A13 (2×) | 26.2% → 28.3% (+2.1 [−1.5, +5.7]) |

- Tool calling drops early in training and recovers by update 36; more training of the same mix does not improve it further.
- More thinking-ON examples that end in a tool call help a little, consistent with the "answer and stop" mechanism. Not tested beyond 2×.

## What did not work

- **Context distillation from v0.1 with an identity system prompt,** for thinking-ON rows: 0 of 200 pilot traces passed QC, even with an instruction not to mention the system prompt.
- **A3 with a forced thinking start as the teacher:** 11 of 200 passed QC.
- **More training** (A9, A11): no identity gain, plus a few other-lab rewrites (for example, "GPT-4 trained by the Marin Community").
- **Less training** (A12): tool calling collapses. It breaks early and recovers by update 36.
- **A tiny Tülu-style set** (A10): weaker identity; it still claims another lab in 9 of 52 thinking-ON answers.
- **Linear merges of A3 and A8a:** no blend gets both A3's BFCL and A8a's clean reasoning.

## Models

A3, A8a and A13 are archived in public HF repos under open-athena, with recipe, data hashes and scores in each card:

- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A3-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A8a-2026.10.30`
- `open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-Identity-PathB-A13-2026.10.30`

issues.body: Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LVfMDHRBKBk_Bn9PY1J9Lb_MYwdUTFP5PkX2br25TNg/edit?tab=t.izhzsywzorld. Final results and the full ledger: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6076348127 (ledger also at https://gist.github.com/karansag/0ce1a07580bd430bc8c5b890069385b0). ## TL;DR (final, 2026-10-09). ** Given **one expert E** ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) built from the Snowball student B ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92 @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) by SFT on [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces, three methods were used to transfer E's gain back into B: * plain SFT on E's traces * SFT on rejection-sampled E traces (RS-SFT) * on-policy distillation from E (OPD). All three recover most or all of E's CruxEval gain on the 1,600 training-is-test prompts (4x sample traces from the test set size). Two-pass CruxEval input / output accuracy on the selected checkpoints: plain SFT 73.9 / 72.0, RS-SFT 80.8 / 77.9, OPD 79.6 / 75.2, against E 79.4 / 71.4 and B 55.4 / 57.8. RS-SFT and OPD are both 3–7 pp above plain SFT; the RS-SFT vs OPD ordering (1.2 / 2.7 pp) is unresolved with one run per arm and two evaluator passes. No arm dropped below B on GSM8K or MATH500. Training cost: plain SFT 61.6 H100-h, RS-SFT 57.4, OPD 376.4 for the full run (286.9 to the selected checkpoint, plus 14–15 per HF export). RS-SFT used ground-truth execution results to select demos; the other arms did not. These numbers measure transfer on seen prompts, not generalization. **Eval policy results (updated 2026-11-06):** the full benchmark tables for this experiment's candidates are in [this comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6665512701) and are updated in place after each reviewed delta. ## Results (selected checkpoints; CruxEval two-pass means, pass@1 %, 800 problems per direction; "gap closed" = gain over B divided by E's gain over B).** | Model | CruxEval input | CruxEval output | Gap closed (in / out) | GSM8K | MATH500 | Training H100-h | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | B ([baseline Snowball student, HF @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) | 55.4 | 57.8 | 0 | 90.4 | 89.8 | — | | [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) (teacher of E; served as `glm-5.3` through the internal glm53 relay, reasoning effort high) | 94.0 | 90.5 | — | — | — | — | | E (expert; B + SFT on GLM traces, step 272; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) | 79.4 | 71.4 | 100% | 92.1 | 92.2 | 35.9 | | Plain SFT on E demos, 400 updates (final; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`)) | 73.9 | 72.0 | 77% / 104% | 94.0 | 92.6 | 61.6 | | RS-SFT on execution-correct E demos, 283 of 376 updates ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`)) | 80.8 | 77.9 | 106% / 148% | 93.5 | 93.6 | 57.4 (full run) | | OPD from E, 75 of 100 updates ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`)) | 79.6 | 75.2 | 101% / 128% | 92.5 | 90.4 | 286.9 to the checkpoint; 376.4 full run; +14–15 per HF export | ## Models Student B = [`open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92` @ `fdc3c3c5`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab) (Hugging Face commit; the repo received a later commit on 2026-10-13, so the pin matters). E = B after full SFT on 1,454 execution-correct [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces (trace collection: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/scratch/karan/glm-bench-traces/`) (LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, 272 updates, 32 H100, fresh optimizer state, frozen router biases), export [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`). E keeps B's tokenizer and chat template. E+ (E + 2 epochs at LR 1e-6; 80.2 / 75.1) was built as a separate reference and is not an arm. Every arm starts from B. ## Benchmark CruxEval (800 Python functions; input prediction and output prediction scored separately by executing the assertion). MATH500 was dropped as the target because B already scores 89.8% there; GSM8K and MATH500 are the collapse checks. Teacher gate: B 55.4 / 57.8; GLM 5.3 on the identical 1,600 prompts 94.0 / 90.5; E 79.4 / 71.4 (two-pass mean), passing the gate of B + 10 points on both tasks with no GSM8K drop. ## Frozen evaluator Marin `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` with Evalchemy [`ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8), vLLM on H100x8 (DP8 + EP8), `max_model_len` 32768, `max_gen_toks` 30720, `enable_thinking: true`, reasoning parser `grug`. Configs and pitfalls: https://gist.github.com/karansag/49de943771b98a7a23d9348b58933f71. Evalchemy's chat client sends no temperature, top_p or seed, and B's `generation_config.json` sets none, so every run samples at vLLM's default (temperature 1.0, unseeded). One pass on 800 problems has a binomial 95% half-width of about 3.5 pp; selected checkpoints get two passes. **Arms as run (all from B; AdamW LR 1e-6 constant, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, grad clip 1.0, router bias frozen; 4 epochs over the 1,600 prompts; one checkpoint per epoch).** - E demos: 8 samples per prompt from E at temperature 1.0, both directions, execution-graded in an isolated container (12,800 samples, 14.6 H100-h, shared by both SFT arms). - Plain SFT: E's first sample per prompt, correct or not (1,600 rows; 1.45M supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16; Levanter, 32 H100). - RS-SFT: first execution-correct sample per prompt (1,503 rows; 97 prompts with no correct sample stay in the eval denominator; 1.06M supervised tokens per epoch; Levanter, 32 H100). - OPD: [MarinSkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL), 4 on-policy rollouts per prompt at temperature 1.0, E as the teacher (sampled reverse KL on chosen tokens, no verifier), 64 prompts per update, 25 updates per epoch; 4 learner + 1 rollout + 1 teacher H100x8 nodes (Megatron). - Selection: the final checkpoint when it is similar or better than the previous one on both CruxEval directions, otherwise a second pass on both and the two-pass means decide. Plain SFT selected its final checkpoint (400 updates); RS-SFT (283 of 376) and OPD (75 of 100) selected their epoch-3 checkpoints after their finals dropped on one direction. ## Artifacts Trace browser (GLM, E, E+ traces, side-by-side compare): https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/072c90b0-281e-4692-a4bf-845874c021b1/. OPD W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/skyrl/runs/p3ie2bg7. Selected exports: plain [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`), RS-SFT [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`), OPD [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`). Eval records: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals//record.json` (every record id is in the final comment's ledger). GPU-hour method: https://gist.github.com/karansag/500604143668730f8e79277b43f39298. ## Not in scope Weight merging (needs RL-trained experts that share B's init; none exist) and transfer from the older Snowball experts (none beats B under the matched eval). ## Decision log - 2026-10-06: matched eval of B and the existing experts (E6, E17a, E18, SWE, Stage-3) on MATH500/GSM8K; none beats B, so no promotion to teacher. - 2026-10-07: MATH500 near ceiling for B → CruxEval chosen; MMLU-Pro (B 44.1) and GPQA-D (B 41.9) measured as fallbacks and not used. - 2026-10-07: full SFT over LoRA for building E; LoRA kept as the fallback if full SFT collapses out-of-domain. - 2026-10-07: rejection-sampled SFT added as a third arm. - 2026-10-08: E frozen at step 272 for every arm; E+ built as a separate reference only. Arms changed from the plan: one sample per prompt for both SFT arms (not up to 4), no LR sweep, 4 rollouts per prompt for OPD. The arms ran in parallel on Iris. - 2026-10-09: RS-SFT and OPD final checkpoints not selected (drops on one direction with paired CI excluding 0); epoch-3 checkpoints selected on two-pass means. Final results posted in one comment; the running-log comments were removed and are archived with the ledger.

- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150) — versioned SkyRL experiment and export contract
- [`experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147) — shared evaluation launch path

# Proposed Fix

1. Follow the submitted teacher retry through a completed update, full training, and verified HF exports. Evaluate the planned exports with the frozen CruxEval/GSM8K configuration. Stop the transfer arms unless E clears the stated +10-point gate on both CruxEval directions without a GSM8K drop beyond noise.
2. Pin E, B, prompt IDs, tokenizer/template, grader, evaluator, and one eight-sample-per-prompt teacher generation artifact. Build unfiltered SFT from samples 1–4 and rejection-sampled SFT from up to four execution-correct samples. Record missing-correct-sample prompts, actual supervised tokens, and teacher-generation GPU-hours; a matched prompt set alone does not equalize training tokens.
3. Start OPD from the same B and prompts. Check teacher/student token-score alignment and one update plus export before the full run. Match the planned sweep and student update budget across arms, and record teacher-scoring GPU-hours separately.
4. Evaluate every selected arm twice with the same pinned evaluator on CruxEval input, CruxEval output, and GSM8K. Report each arm's accuracy, `(arm − B) / (E − B)` per direction, run-to-run spread, prompts and tokens consumed, and total GPU-hours. Label gains as transfer on the trained test prompts; this protocol cannot establish held-out generalization.
